title.zh: 卷十八 魏書十八 二李臧文呂許典二龐閻傳
title.en: Volume 18: Book of Wei 18 - Biographies of the two Lis, Zang, Wen, Lü, Xu, Dian, the two Pangs, and Yan
title.raw: 卷十八 魏書十八 二李臧文呂許典二龐閻傳 Volume 18: Book of Wei 18 - Biographies of the two Lis, Zang, Wen, Lü, Xu, Dian, the two Pangs, and Yan

sentences.zh: 李典 李通 臧霸 文聘 吕虔 许褚 典韦 庞德 庞淯 阎温

translations.literal: Li Dian, Li Tong, Zang Ba, Wen Pin, Lü Qian, Xu Chu, Dian Wei, Pang De, Pang Jun, Yan Wen.
translations.idiomatic: This scroll groups the biographies of Li Dian, Li Tong, Zang Ba, Wen Pin, Lü Qian, Xu Chu, Dian Wei, Pang De, Pang Jun, and Yan Wen.

sentences.zh: 李典字曼成，山阳钜野人也。

translations.literal: Li Dian, courtesy name Mancheng, was a man of Juye in Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dian, whose courtesy name was Mancheng, came from Juye in Shanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 典从父乾，有雄气，合宾客数千家在乘氏。

translations.literal: Dian's father's younger brother Qian had a heroic temper and gathered several thousand client households at Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Li Qian was a man of bold spirit who had assembled several thousand dependent families at Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 初平中，以众随太祖，破黄巾於寿张，又从击袁术，征徐州。

translations.literal: In the Chuping years he brought his followers to Cao Cao, defeated the Yellow Turbans at Shouzhang, followed him against Yuan Shu, and campaigned in Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuping era he joined Cao Cao with his band, helped smash the Yellow Turbans at Shouzhang, served against Yuan Shu, and took part in the Xu Province campaigns.

sentences.zh: 吕布之乱，太祖遣乾还乘氏，慰劳诸县。

translations.literal: During Lü Bu's revolt Cao Cao sent Qian back to Chengshi to console the counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Bu rose in revolt, Cao Cao sent Li Qian home to Chengshi to reassure the local counties.

sentences.zh: 布别驾薛兰、治中李封招乾，欲俱叛，乾不听，遂杀乾。

translations.literal: Lü Bu's aide Xue Lan and administrator Li Feng summoned Qian to rebel with them; Qian refused, so they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's staff officers Xue Lan and Li Feng tried to win Li Qian over to rebellion; he refused, and they murdered him.

sentences.zh: 太祖使乾子整将乾兵，与诸将击兰、封。

translations.literal: Cao Cao ordered Qian's son Zheng to command Qian's troops and join the generals against Lan and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao put Li Qian's son Li Zheng at the head of his father's force to join the other generals against Xue Lan and Li Feng.

sentences.zh: 兰、封破，从平兗州诸县有功，稍迁青州刺史。

translations.literal: When Lan and Feng were broken, he followed in pacifying the Yanzhou counties with merit and was gradually promoted to Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Xue Lan and Li Feng were destroyed, he helped pacify Yanzhou and rose step by step to inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 整卒，典徙颍阴令，为中郎将，将整军，

translations.literal: When Zheng died, Dian was transferred to magistrate of Yingyin, became a general of the household, and commanded Zheng's army,
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zheng died, Li Dian became magistrate of Yingyin and a general of the household, taking command of Li Zheng's troops,

sentences.zh: 〈《魏书》曰：典少好学，不乐兵事，乃就师读《春秋左氏传》，博观群书。

translations.literal: The Wei shu says: In youth Dian loved study and did not delight in soldiering; he sought a teacher and read the Zuo commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, and read widely among the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei records that Li Dian loved books as a young man and disliked war; he apprenticed himself to read the Zuo zhuan and ranged widely through other texts.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之，故试以治民之政。〉

translations.literal: Cao Cao approved of this, and therefore tried him with civil administration.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao approved and deliberately tested him in civil office.

sentences.zh: 迁离狐太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be governor of Lihu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Lihu commandery.

sentences.zh: 时太祖与袁绍相拒官渡，典率宗族及部曲输谷帛供军。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao faced Yuan Shao at Guandu, Dian led his clan and private retainers to ship grain and silk for the army.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao held the line at Guandu against Yuan Shao, Li Dian convoyed grain and cloth for the army with his kinsmen and household troops.

sentences.zh: 绍破，以典为裨将军，屯安民。

translations.literal: When Shao was defeated, Dian was appointed major general and garrisoned Anmin.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Shao's defeat he was named major general and posted to Anmin.

sentences.zh: 太祖击谭、尚於黎阳，使典与程昱等以船运军粮。

translations.literal: Cao Cao attacked Tan and Shang at Liyang and ordered Dian with Cheng Yu and others to transport army grain by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao struck Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang at Liyang and ordered Li Dian and Cheng Yu to move supplies by river.

sentences.zh: 会尚遣魏郡太守高蕃将兵屯河上，绝水道，太祖敕典、昱：“若船不得过，下从陆道。

translations.literal: It happened that Shang sent the Wei commandery governor Gao Fan with troops to hold the river and cut the waterway; Cao Cao instructed Dian and Yu: "If the boats cannot pass, come down to the land route."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang sent the governor of Wei, Gao Fan, to block the river; Cao Cao told Li Dian and Cheng Yu that if the convoy could not get through they should shift to a land route.

sentences.zh: ”典与诸将议曰：“蕃军少甲而恃水，有懈怠之心，击之必克。

translations.literal: Dian consulted the generals and said: "Fan's troops are few in armor yet trust to the water; they are slack at heart—a strike will surely take them. Troops in the field need not wait on orders from the rear; if it serves the state, one may act on one's own authority—we should attack at once."
translations.idiomatic: Li Dian urged his colleagues, "Gao Fan is lightly armored and overconfident behind the river—he can be overrun. In the field a commander who sees a chance for the realm need not wait on capital orders. We should hit him now."

sentences.zh: 军不内御；

translations.literal: Troops in the field are not commanded from the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: An army on campaign cannot wait for every order from the rear.

sentences.zh: 苟利国家，专之可也，宜亟击之。

translations.literal: If it profits the state, concentrating decision in the field is permissible—it is right to strike urgently.
translations.idiomatic: When the common good is at stake, a forward commander may act on his own—we should move immediately.

sentences.zh: ”昱亦以为然。

translations.literal: Yu also agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂北渡河，攻蕃，破之，水道得通。

translations.literal: They crossed the river north, attacked Fan, defeated him, and the waterway was opened.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed to the north bank, smashed Gao Fan, and reopened the supply line.

sentences.zh: 刘表使刘备北侵，至叶，太祖遣典从夏侯惇拒之。

translations.literal: Liu Biao sent Liu Bei to raid north as far as Ye; Cao Cao ordered Dian to follow Xiahou Dun and resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao sent Liu Bei north as far as Ye; Cao Cao detached Li Dian to serve under Xiahou Dun against him.

sentences.zh: 备一旦烧屯去，惇率诸军追击之，典曰：“贼无故退，疑必有伏。

translations.literal: Bei one morning burned his camps and withdrew; Dun led the armies in pursuit. Dian said: "The enemy has withdrawn for no clear reason—I suspect an ambush. The southern road is narrow and the growth is deep—we must not pursue."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei burned his camps overnight and slipped away; Xiahou Dun gave chase. Li Dian warned, "A retreat without battle smells of ambush. The southern track is narrow and overgrown—we should not follow."

sentences.zh: 南道狭窄，草木深，不可追也。

translations.literal: The southern road is narrow and the vegetation deep—it is not possible to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: The defile is tight and the brush thick—a pursuit would be reckless.

sentences.zh: ”惇不听，与于禁追之，典留守。

translations.literal: Dun would not listen; with Yu Jin he pursued, while Dian remained to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Dun refused to listen and went ahead with Yu Jin, leaving Li Dian to hold the camp.

sentences.zh: 惇等果入贼伏里，战不利，典往救，备望见救至，乃散退。

translations.literal: Dun and the others indeed walked into an ambush; the battle went badly until Dian came to the rescue; Bei saw reinforcements arrive and broke off.
translations.idiomatic: They walked into Liu Bei's trap; Li Dian's counterattack broke the encirclement and Liu Bei withdrew when he saw relief arrive.

sentences.zh: 从围鄴，鄴定，与乐进围高幹於壶关，击管承於长广，皆破之。

translations.literal: He followed in besieging Ye; when Ye was settled, with Yue Jin he besieged Gao Gan at Huguan and struck Guan Cheng at Changguang—all were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the siege of Ye, then with Yue Jin invested Gao Gan at Huguan and campaigned against Guan Cheng in Changguang, winning both actions.

sentences.zh: 迁捕虏将军，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted to general who captures bandits and enfeoffed as marquis of the metropolitan village.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who captures bandits and received a village marquisate at the capital.

sentences.zh: 典宗族部曲三千餘家，居乘氏，自请原徙诣魏郡。

translations.literal: Dian's clan and private households, more than three thousand families, lived at Chengshi; he asked permission to move them wholesale into Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand households of his clan and retainers lived at Chengshi; he asked to relocate them all into Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 太祖笑曰：“卿欲慕耿纯邪？

translations.literal: Cao Cao laughed and said: "Do you wish to imitate Geng Chun?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao laughed and asked whether he meant to imitate Geng Chun's famous resettlement of his clan.

sentences.zh: ”典谢曰：“典驽怯功微，而爵宠过厚，诚宜举宗陈力；

translations.literal: Dian apologized: "Dian is dull and timid, my merit slight yet rank and favor are too heavy—I truly ought to move the whole clan to exert its strength; moreover with campaigning unceased, it is right to fill the inner districts around the capital to brace the four quarters—it is not admiration of Chun."
translations.idiomatic: Li Dian bowed and said, "I am a mediocre soldier who has received too much honor; I wish to bring my people closer so they may serve you. With war still raging, strengthening the heartland steadies the frontiers—this is not mere imitation of Geng Chun."

sentences.zh: 加以征伐未息，宜实郊遂之内，以制四方，非慕纯也。

translations.literal: Moreover with campaigning unceased, it is right to settle the inner approaches to control the four quarters—it is not that I admire Chun.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland must be stocked while armies are in the field; my purpose is practical, not sentimental.

sentences.zh: ”遂徙部曲宗族万三千餘口居鄴。

translations.literal: Thereupon he moved more than thirteen thousand mouths of retainers and kin to dwell at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore moved more than thirteen thousand followers and relatives to Ye.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，迁破虏将军。

translations.literal: Cao Cao praised him and promoted him to general who breaks bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao commended him and named him general who breaks bandits.

sentences.zh: 与张辽、乐进屯合肥，孙权率众围之，辽欲奉教出战。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Liao and Yue Jin he garrisoned Hefei; Sun Quan led a host to besiege them, and Liao wished to follow the sealed orders and sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Liao and Yue Jin he held Hefei when Sun Quan brought a great army; Zhang Liao meant to obey Cao Cao's order and sortie.

sentences.zh: 进、典、辽皆素不睦，辽恐其不从，典慨然曰：“此国家大事，顾君计何如耳，吾可以私憾而忘公义乎！

translations.literal: Jin, Dian, and Liao had long been on poor terms; Liao feared they would not follow, but Dian said spiritedly: "This is the great affair of the state—I look only to your plan; could I let private resentment forget public duty!"
translations.idiomatic: The three had never been friends, and Zhang Liao feared Li Dian would balk; Li Dian declared, "This is the state's crisis, not a private quarrel—I will follow your plan."

sentences.zh: ”乃率众与辽破走权。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his troops with Liao to defeat and rout Quan.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men with Zhang Liao and helped drive Sun Quan from the walls.

sentences.zh: 增邑百户，并前三百户。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by one hundred households; together with the previous total it came to three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: His fief rose by a hundred households to three hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 典好学问，贵儒雅，不与诸将争功。

translations.literal: Dian loved learning, honored refined scholars, and did not wrangle over merit with the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dian loved books, respected literati, and never wrangled for credit with fellow commanders.

sentences.zh: 敬贤士大夫，恂恂若不及，军中称其长者。

translations.literal: He respected worthy gentlemen and was modest as if he could never catch up; the army called him an elder statesman.
translations.idiomatic: He treated scholars with deference and carried himself with modesty; the troops called him the elder among them.

sentences.zh: 年三十六薨，子祯嗣。

translations.literal: At age thirty-six he died; his son Zhen inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-six, and his son Li Zhen inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 文帝践阼，追念合肥之功，增祯邑百户，赐典一子爵关内侯，邑百户；

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, remembering the Hefei achievement, he increased Zhen's fief by one hundred households, granted one of Dian's sons a secondary marquisate of one hundred households,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, remembering Hefei, added a hundred households to Li Zhen's fief and enfeoffed one of Li Dian's sons as a secondary marquis with another hundred households,

sentences.zh: 谥典曰愍侯。

translations.literal: and gave Dian the posthumous title Marquis Min.
translations.idiomatic: and posthumously titled Li Dian Marquis Min, "the Pitiable."

sentences.zh: 李通字文达，江夏平春人也。

translations.literal: Li Tong, courtesy name Wendao, was a man of Pingchun in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong, courtesy name Wendao, was a native of Pingchun in Jiangxia commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：通小字万亿。〉

translations.literal: The Wei lüe says: Tong's childhood name was Wanyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe gives his childhood name as Wanyi.

sentences.zh: 以侠闻於江、汝之间。

translations.literal: He was famed as a knight-errant between the Yangtze and the Ru.
translations.idiomatic: He was known as a man of chivalry between the Yangtze and the Ru rivers.

sentences.zh: 与其郡人陈恭共起兵於朗陵，众多归之。

translations.literal: Together with his townsman Chen Gong he raised troops at Langling, and a great multitude joined them.
translations.idiomatic: He and his fellow townsman Chen Gong raised force at Langling, and thousands rallied to them.

sentences.zh: 时有周直者，众二千餘家，与恭、通外和内违。

translations.literal: At that time there was one Zhou Zhi with more than two thousand households who outwardly agreed with Gong and Tong but inwardly opposed them.
translations.idiomatic: A local leader named Zhou Zhi commanded more than two thousand households and feigned alliance while plotting against them.

sentences.zh: 通欲图杀直而恭难之。

translations.literal: Tong wished to plot killing Zhi but Gong hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong meant to eliminate Zhou Zhi, but Chen Gong shrank from the deed.

sentences.zh: 通知恭无断，乃独定策，与直克会，酒酣杀直。

translations.literal: Seeing that Gong lacked resolution, Tong alone fixed a plan, met Zhi at a banquet, and when the wine ran high slew Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Chen Gong's indecision, Li Tong arranged a parley, drank with Zhou Zhi, and cut him down when the cups had gone round.

sentences.zh: 众人大扰，通率恭诛其党帅，尽并其营。

translations.literal: The crowd was thrown into confusion; Tong led Gong in executing their chieftains and annexed their entire camp.
translations.idiomatic: The camp erupted in confusion; Li Tong led Chen Gong in killing the ringleaders and absorbed every follower.

sentences.zh: 后恭妻弟陈郃，杀恭而据其众。

translations.literal: Later Gong's wife's younger brother Chen He killed Gong and seized his following.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chen He, Chen Gong's brother-in-law, murdered Chen Gong and seized his men.

sentences.zh: 通攻破郃军，斩郃首以祭恭墓。

translations.literal: Tong broke He's army, beheaded He, and offered the head at Gong's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong shattered Chen He's force, took his head, and sacrificed it at Chen Gong's grave.

sentences.zh: 又生禽黄巾大帅吴霸而降其属。

translations.literal: He also captured alive the Yellow Turban grand chieftain Wu Ba and brought his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Yellow Turban leader Wu Ba alive and brought the whole band to submission.

sentences.zh: 遭岁大饥，通倾家振施，与士分糟糠，皆争为用，由是盗贼不敢犯。

translations.literal: A year of great famine came; Tong exhausted his household to relieve others, sharing chaff and husks with his men, so that all strove to serve him—therefore bandits did not dare molest him.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine he emptied his granaries for relief, shared the coarsest fare with his followers, and won such loyalty that outlaws dared not trouble his district.

sentences.zh: 建安初，通举众诣太祖於许。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jian'an, Tong led his multitude to Cao Cao at Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jian'an era he brought his following to Cao Cao at Xu.

sentences.zh: 拜通振威中郎将，屯汝南西界。

translations.literal: Tong was appointed general of the household who shakes might and garrisoned the western border of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He was named general of the household who shakes might and posted to Runan's western frontier.

sentences.zh: 太祖讨张绣，刘表遣兵以助绣，太祖军不利。

translations.literal: Cao Cao campaigned against Zhang Xiu; Liu Biao sent troops to aid Xiu, and Cao Cao's army fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao attacked Zhang Xiu, Liu Biao reinforced Zhang Xiu and Cao Cao's army was thrown back.

sentences.zh: 通将兵夜诣太祖，太祖得以复战，通为先登，大破绣军。

translations.literal: Tong led troops by night to Cao Cao, enabling him to renew the battle; Tong was first on the wall and greatly broke Xiu's army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong marched by night to Cao Cao's aid, spearheaded the counterattack, and shattered Zhang Xiu's line.

sentences.zh: 拜裨将军，封建功侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed major general and enfeoffed as marquis who establishes merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to major general and enfeoffed as marquis who establishes merit.

sentences.zh: 分汝南二县，以通为阳安都尉。

translations.literal: Two counties of Runan were split off and Tong made chief commandant who pacifies the south.
translations.idiomatic: Two Runan counties were set aside for him as chief commandant who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 通妻伯父犯法，朗陵长赵俨收治，致之大辟。

translations.literal: Tong's wife's uncle broke the law; the Langling magistrate Zhao Yan arrested and tried him, sentencing him to death.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's uncle broke the law; Zhao Yan, magistrate of Langling, arrested him and sought the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 是时杀生之柄，决於牧守，通妻子号泣以请其命。

translations.literal: At that time the power of life and death lay with the regional governor; Tong's wife and children wept to beg for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors then held final say over executions; Li Tong's family wept and begged for the man's life.

sentences.zh: 通曰：“方与曹公戮力，义不以私废公。

translations.literal: Tong said: "I am striving with Lord Cao on the same rope—righteousness does not allow private feeling to overturn the public good."
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong said, "I am pledged to Cao Cao; private ties cannot overturn the law."

sentences.zh: ”嘉俨执宪不阿，与为亲交。

translations.literal: He praised Yan for upholding the code without bending and became his sworn friend.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Zhao Yan's integrity and became his close friend.

sentences.zh: 太祖与袁绍相拒於官渡。

translations.literal: Cao Cao faced Yuan Shao at Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao held Guandu against Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 绍遣使拜通征南将军，刘表亦阴招之，通皆拒焉。

translations.literal: Shao sent an envoy to appoint Tong general who campaigns south, and Liu Biao also secretly summoned him; Tong refused both.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent an envoy naming him general who campaigns south, and Liu Biao secretly wooed him as well; Li Tong refused every overture.

sentences.zh: 通亲戚部曲流涕曰：“今孤危独守，以失大援，亡可立而待也，不如亟从绍。

translations.literal: Tong's kinsmen and retainers wept and said: "Now we stand alone in peril and have lost great support—destruction can arrive in a moment—it is better urgently to follow Shao."
translations.idiomatic: His clansmen wept that isolation would destroy them unless he sided with Yuan Shao at once.

sentences.zh: ”通按剑以叱之曰：“曹公明哲，必定天下。

translations.literal: Tong grasped his sword and rebuked them: "Lord Cao is wise and will surely settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword and swore, "Cao Cao is clear-sighted and will pacify the empire.

sentences.zh: 绍虽强盛，而任使无方，终为之虏耳。

translations.literal: Shao may be strong for the moment, yet he employs men without method—in the end he will be their captive.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao is strong but cannot use men; he will end as someone else's prisoner.

sentences.zh: 吾以死不贰。

translations.literal: I mean to die without a second allegiance."
translations.idiomatic: I will die before I serve another."

sentences.zh: ”即斩绍使，送印绶诣太祖。

translations.literal: He immediately beheaded Shao's envoy and sent the seals and ribbons to Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Yuan Shao's envoy on the spot and forwarded the insignia to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 又击郡贼瞿恭、江宫、沈成等，皆破残其众，送其首。

translations.literal: He also struck the commandery bandits Qu Gong, Jiang Gong, Shen Cheng, and others, broke and scattered their hosts, and sent their heads.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed local bandits Qu Gong, Jiang Gong, and Shen Cheng, scattered their bands, and sent in their heads.

sentences.zh: 遂定淮、汝之地。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Huai and Ru regions were settled.
translations.idiomatic: The country between the Huai and the Ru was pacified.

sentences.zh: 改封都亭侯，拜汝南太守。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to village marquis at the capital and he was appointed governor of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to a capital village marquisate and made governor of Runan.

sentences.zh: 时贼张赤等五千餘家聚桃山，通攻破之。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit Zhang Chi and more than five thousand households gathered at Peach Mountain; Tong broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chi and five thousand families held Peach Mountain, Li Tong overran their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 昔侍坐於先帝，时有三长吏俱见。

translations.literal: Formerly I attended the late emperor in audience when three senior clerks were received together.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when I sat in attendance on the late emperor, three senior officials were received together.

sentences.zh: 临辞出，上曰：‘为官长当清，当慎，当勤，修此三者，何患不治乎？

translations.literal: As they took leave, the sovereign said: "As a magistrate one must be incorrupt, cautious, and diligent; cultivate these three—why fear misrule?"
translations.idiomatic: At their departure he told them, "A magistrate must be clean, careful, and industrious; master those three and good order follows."

sentences.zh: ’并受诏。

translations.literal: They all received the charge.
translations.idiomatic: All three accepted the lesson.

sentences.zh: 既出，上顾谓吾等曰：‘相诫敕正当尔不？

translations.literal: After they left, the sovereign turned to us and said: "Did my admonition hit the mark?"
translations.idiomatic: When they had gone, he turned to the rest of us and asked whether his counsel had been apt.

sentences.zh: ’侍坐众贤，莫不赞善。

translations.literal: The worthy men who sat in attendance all praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Every man present praised his words.

sentences.zh: 上又问曰：‘必不得已，於斯三者何先？

translations.literal: He asked again: "If one must choose among the three, which comes first?"
translations.idiomatic: He pressed further: if one had to rank the three, which should lead?

sentences.zh: ’或对曰：‘清固为本。

translations.literal: Someone answered: "Incorruptibility is surely the root."
translations.idiomatic: One replied that incorruptibility must be the root.

sentences.zh: ’次复问吾，对曰：‘清慎之道，相须而成，必不得已，慎乃为大。

translations.literal: He next asked me; I answered: "The ways of cleanliness and caution need each other; if one must choose, caution is the greater.
translations.idiomatic: When he asked me, I said caution mattered most when the two could not be divided.

sentences.zh: 夫清者不必慎，慎者必自清，亦由仁者必有勇，勇者不必有仁，是以易称括囊无咎，藉用白茅，皆慎之至也。

translations.literal: The incorrupt need not always be cautious, yet the cautious are always clean; just as the humane surely have courage while the courageous need not be humane—thus the Changes speaks of tying the sack without blame and offering on white rushes, both utmost caution."
translations.idiomatic: A scrupulous man need not be spotless, but a careful man ends clean, as courage may follow humanity though courage alone is not humanity; the classic images of the tied sack and the white rushes are images of supreme care."

sentences.zh: ’上曰：‘卿言得之耳。

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "You have grasped it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said I had the right of it.

sentences.zh: 可举近世能慎者谁乎？

translations.literal: "Name the most cautious men of recent times."
translations.idiomatic: He asked who in recent times had shown such care.

sentences.zh: ’诸人各未知所对，吾乃举故太尉荀景倩、尚书董仲连、仆射王公仲并可谓为慎。

translations.literal: Each man did not know how to answer; I named the late Grand Commandant Xun Jingqian, Minister Dong Zhonglian, and Director Wang Gongzhong as examples of caution.
translations.idiomatic: No one spoke until I named the late Xun Jingqian, Dong Zhonglian, and Wang Gongzhong as men of true caution.

sentences.zh: 上曰：‘此诸人者，温恭朝夕，执事有恪，亦各其慎也。

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "Those men are mild and reverent from dawn to dusk and conscientious in office—each in his way is cautious.
translations.idiomatic: He replied that those officials were diligent and deferential day and night—each was cautious in his office.

sentences.zh: 然天下之至慎，其惟阮嗣宗乎！

translations.literal: Yet the most cautious man in the realm is surely Ruan Sizong!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the most cautious man in the realm, he said, was Ruan Ji.

sentences.zh: 每与之言，言及玄远，而未曾评论时事，臧否人物，真可谓至慎矣。

translations.literal: Whenever one spoke with him, he reached only to abstruse topics and never judged current affairs or praised or blamed individuals—truly he may be called supremely cautious."
translations.idiomatic: In every conversation Ruan Ji kept to lofty themes and never touched current events or passed judgment on men—there lay supreme caution."

sentences.zh: ’吾每思此言，亦足以为明诫。

translations.literal: I often think on those words—they are enough for a clear warning.
translations.idiomatic: I have often recalled that exchange as a mirror for conduct.

sentences.zh: 凡人行事，年少立身，不可不慎，勿轻论人，勿轻说事，如此则悔吝何由而生，患祸无从而至矣。

translations.literal: In all human conduct, in youth establishing oneself, one must be cautious: do not lightly discuss others or lightly speak of affairs—thus regret and misfortune have no gate to enter and disaster has no path to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In youth one must be careful not to gossip about men or affairs lightly; then regret and calamity find no opening.

sentences.zh: 〈秉子重，字茂曾。

translations.literal: Bing's son Chong, courtesy name Maozeng.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's son Li Chong, courtesy name Maozeng,

sentences.zh: 少知名，历位吏部郎、平阳太守。

translations.literal: In youth he was known; he rose to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and governor of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: won early fame and rose to personnel director and governor of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 晋诸公赞曰：重以清尚称。

translations.literal: The Jin zhugong zan says: Chong was praised for purity and high principle.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin zhugong zan praises him for purity and integrity.

sentences.zh: 相国赵王伦以重望取为右司马。

translations.literal: Prince-regent Zhao Wang Lun of the realm took him as right marshal for his prestige.
translations.idiomatic: The prince-regent Sima Lun took him as right marshal for his reputation.

sentences.zh: 重以伦将为乱，辞疾不就。

translations.literal: Chong saw that Lun would bring disorder and pleaded illness to decline office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong saw Sima Lun's coup coming and declined appointment on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 伦逼之不已，重遂不复自活，至於困笃，扶曳受拜，数日卒，赠散骑常侍。

translations.literal: Lun pressed him without cease; Chong thereupon gave up caring for his life until he was gravely ill, was helped forward to accept the commission, and died within days; he was posthumously honored as regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun hounded him until Li Chong let his health fail, was carried in to take the post, and died within days; the court mourned him as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 重二弟，尚字茂仲，矩字茂约，永嘉中并典郡；

translations.literal: Chong had two younger brothers: Shang, courtesy Maozhong, and Ju, courtesy Maoyue; in the Yongjia years both governed commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Li Shang and Li Ju, courtesy names Maozhong and Maoyue, both held prefectures in the Yongjia era;

sentences.zh: 矩至江州刺史。

translations.literal: Ju reached the office of Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju rose to become inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 重子式，字景则，官至侍中。〉

translations.literal: Chong's son Shi, courtesy name Jingze, reached office as palace attendant.〉
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Shi, courtesy name Jingze, rose to palace attendant.〉

sentences.zh: 臧霸字宣高，泰山华人也。

translations.literal: Zang Ba, courtesy name Xuangao, was a man of Hua in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba, courtesy name Xuangao, came from Hua county in Taishan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父戒，为县狱掾，据法不听太守欲所私杀。

translations.literal: His father Jie was jail clerk of the county; holding to the law he would not heed the governor's wish to kill privately.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zang Jie served as county jail clerk and refused the governor's unlawful order to execute a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 太守大怒，令收戒诣府，时送者百餘人。

translations.literal: The governor in great rage ordered Jie seized and brought to the headquarters; at the time there were more than a hundred escorts.
translations.idiomatic: The furious governor had Zang Jie arrested and marched to his yamen under escort of over a hundred armed men.

sentences.zh: 霸年十八，将客数十人径於费西山中要夺之，送者莫敢动，因与父俱亡命东海，由是以勇壮闻。

translations.literal: Ba at age eighteen led several tens of retainers straight to intercept and snatch him in the Fei west mountains; the escorts none dared move, and he fled with his father to their lives to Donghai—thereby he became famed for courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen Zang Ba ambushed the escort in the hills west of Fei with dozens of followers, freed his father, and fled with him to Donghai, winning a reputation for valor.

sentences.zh: 黄巾起，霸从陶谦击破之，拜骑都尉。

translations.literal: When the Yellow Turbans arose, Ba followed Tao Qian and defeated them; he was appointed colonel of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Tao Qian against the Yellow Turbans and was named colonel of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 遂收兵於徐州，与孙观、吴敦、尹礼等并聚众，霸为帅，屯於开阳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered troops in Xu Province; together with Sun Guan, Wu Dun, Yin Li, and others they jointly gathered a host, Ba was commander, and they garrisoned at Kaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He collected forces in Xu Province with Sun Guan, Wu Dun, and Yin Li, led them as chieftain, and based them at Kaiyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖之讨吕布也，霸等将兵助布。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Lü Bu, Ba and others led troops to aid Bu.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao attacked Lü Bu, Zang Ba sent troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 既禽布，霸自匿。

translations.literal: After Bu was captured, Ba hid himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Bu fell, Zang Ba went into hiding.

sentences.zh: 太祖募索得霸，见而悦之，使霸招吴敦、尹礼、孙观、观兄康等，皆诣太祖。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor offered a reward and sought and obtained Ba; seeing him he was pleased and ordered Ba to summon Wu Dun, Yin Li, Sun Guan, and Guan's elder brother Kang—all came to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had him found, received him gladly, and sent him to bring in Wu Dun, Yin Li, Sun Guan, and Sun Kang.

sentences.zh: 太祖以霸为琅邪相，敦利城、礼东莞、观北海、康城阳太守，割青、徐二州，委之於霸。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor made Ba chancellor of Langya, Dun governor of Licheng, Li governor of Dongguan, Guan governor of the North Sea, Kang governor of Chengyang, carving off Qing and Xu two provinces and entrusting them to Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao named him chancellor of Langya and parcelled Qing and Xu posts among his allies.

sentences.zh: 太祖之在兗州，以徐翕、毛晖为将。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor was in Yan Province, he made Xu Xi and Mao Hui generals.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao held Yanzhou he appointed Xu Xi and Mao Hui as generals.

sentences.zh: 兗州乱，翕、晖皆叛。

translations.literal: When Yan Province was in turmoil, Xi and Hui both rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhou erupted in revolt, both men mutinied.

sentences.zh: 后兗州定，翕、晖亡命投霸。

translations.literal: After Yan Province was settled, Xi and Hui fled for their lives to Ba.
translations.idiomatic: After order returned they fled for refuge to Zang Ba.

sentences.zh: 太祖语刘备，令语霸送二人首。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor told Liu Bei, ordering Bei to tell Ba to send the two men's heads.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked Liu Bei to demand the heads of Xu Xi and Mao Hui.

sentences.zh: 霸谓备曰：“霸所以能自立者，以不为此也。

translations.literal: Ba said to Bei: "The reason Ba can stand on my own is that I have not done such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba told Liu Bei that his independence rested on refusing such betrayals.

sentences.zh: 霸受公生全之恩，不敢违命。

translations.literal: Ba has received from the duke the grace of saving my life—I dare not disobey the order.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he owed Cao Cao his life and could not openly defy the order.

sentences.zh: 然王霸之君可以义告，原将军为之辞。

translations.literal: Yet lords who aspire to kingship may be addressed with righteousness; I beg the general to speak for me.
translations.idiomatic: A hegemon who aims at true kingship will listen to reason; he asked Liu Bei to intercede.

sentences.zh: ”备以霸言白太祖，太祖叹息，谓霸曰：“此古人之事而君能行之，孤之原也。

translations.literal: Bei reported Ba's words to the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor sighed and said to Ba: "This was an affair of the ancients—yet you, lord, can practice it—that is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei relayed the plea; Cao Cao sighed and praised conduct worthy of antiquity.

sentences.zh: ”乃皆以翕、晖为郡守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made both Xi and Hui commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Xu Xi and Mao Hui as magistrates instead of executing them.

sentences.zh: 时太祖方与袁绍相拒，而霸数以精兵入青州，故太祖得专事绍，不以东方为念。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Progenitor was still facing Yuan Shao, but Ba repeatedly sent crack troops into Qing Province, therefore the Grand Progenitor was able to devote himself solely to Shao and not worry about the east.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao faced Yuan Shao, Zang Ba's raids into Qingzhou pinned eastern enemies so Cao Cao could concentrate on the north.

sentences.zh: 太祖破袁谭於南皮，霸等会贺。

translations.literal: After the Grand Progenitor defeated Yuan Tan at Nanpi, Ba and others assembled to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Nanpi they came to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 霸因求遣子弟及诸将父兄家属诣鄴，太祖曰：“诸君忠孝，岂复在是！

translations.literal: Ba therefore asked to send sons and brothers of the generals and fathers and elder brothers of households to Ye; the Grand Progenitor said: "Gentlemen's loyalty and filial piety—does it rest on this!
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba asked to send hostages to Ye; Cao Cao replied that loyalty and filial piety did not require hostages.

sentences.zh: 昔萧何遣子弟入侍，而高祖不拒，耿纯焚室舆榇以从，而光武不逆，吾将何以易之哉！

translations.literal: Formerly Xiao He sent sons and younger brothers to attend court, yet Gaozu did not refuse; Geng Chun burned his house and brought his coffin to follow, yet Guangwu did not turn away—how shall I change from them!"
translations.idiomatic: He cited Xiao He and Geng Chun as precedents for refusing hostages.

sentences.zh: ”东州扰攘，霸等执义征暴，清定海岱，功莫大焉，皆封列侯。

translations.literal: The eastern provinces were in turmoil; Ba and others grasped righteousness and campaigned against violence, pacifying the sea and Dai—none had greater merit; all were enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: They pacified the Shandong coast and were all enfeoffed as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 霸为都亭侯，加威虏将军。

translations.literal: Ba was metropolitan village marquis and added general who awes bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba received a village marquisate at the capital and the added title general who awes bandits.

sentences.zh: 又与于禁讨昌豨，与夏侯渊讨黄巾餘贼徐和等，有功，迁徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Again together with Yu Jin he campaigned against Chang Xi, and together with Xiahou Yuan against the Yellow Turban remnant bandits Xu He and others; he had merit and was transferred to Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: With Yu Jin he fought Chang Xi, with Xiahou Yuan the Yellow Turban remnants, and was promoted to inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 沛国

translations.literal: Pei princedom.
translations.idiomatic: The narrative turns to events in the princedom of Pei.

translations.literal: (gong) — marginal gloss on the preceding place name.
translations.idiomatic: An editorial gloss reads gong for the place name above.

sentences.zh: 武周为下邳令，霸敬异周，身诣令舍。

translations.literal: Wu Zhou was magistrate of Xiapi; Ba respected Zhou as extraordinary and personally went to the magistrate's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He esteemed Magistrate Wu Zhou of Xiapi and visited his office in person.

sentences.zh: 部从事总詷不法，周得其罪，便收考竟，霸益以善周。

translations.literal: The department clerk had denounced unlawful conduct; Zhou obtained proof of his guilt and thereupon arrested and examined him to the end; Ba all the more considered Zhou good.
translations.idiomatic: When a staff investigator denounced a corrupt clerk, Wu Zhou jailed and tried the man to the end, and Zang Ba admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 从讨孙权，先登，再入巢湖，攻居巢，破之。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Sun Quan, was first to ascend, again entered Chaohu, attacked Juchao, and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Sun Quan, spearheaded the advance into Lake Chao, stormed Juchao, and took it.

sentences.zh: 张辽之讨陈兰，霸别遣至皖，讨吴将韩当，使权不得救兰。

translations.literal: When Zhang Liao campaigned against Chen Lan, Ba separately was dispatched to Wan to campaign against Wu general Han Dang, causing Quan unable to rescue Lan.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhang Liao besieged Chen Lan, Zang Ba struck Han Dang at Wan so Sun Quan could not relieve Chen Lan.

sentences.zh: 当遣兵逆霸，霸与战於逢龙，当复遣兵邀霸於夹石，与战破之，还屯舒。

translations.literal: Dang sent troops to oppose Ba; Ba with him fought at Fenglong; Dang again sent troops to intercept Ba at Jiashi; with them he fought and defeated them, returned and garrisoned Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Han Dang at Fenglong and at Jiashi, then withdrew to garrison Shu.

sentences.zh: 权遣数万人乘船屯舒口，分兵救兰，闻霸军在舒，遁还。

translations.literal: Quan dispatched several tens of thousands of men by boat to garrison at Shu mouth, dividing troops to rescue Lan; hearing Ba's army was at Shu, they fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent a fleet toward Shu to relieve Chen Lan but turned back when he learned Zang Ba held Shu.

sentences.zh: 霸夜追之，比明，行百餘里，邀贼前后击之。

translations.literal: Ba pursued them by night; by dawn he had gone more than a hundred li, intercepting the bandits front and rear and striking them.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba pursued through the night, over a hundred li by dawn, and hit the enemy vanguard and rear.

sentences.zh: 贼窘急，不得上船，赴水者甚众。

translations.literal: The bandits were pressed and urgent, could not board ships, and very many threw themselves into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped, many drowned trying to reach their boats.

sentences.zh: 由是贼不得救兰，辽遂破之。

translations.literal: Thereby the bandits could not rescue Lan, and Liao thereupon broke them.
translations.idiomatic: They never reached Chen Lan, and Zhang Liao crushed him.

sentences.zh: 霸从讨孙权於濡须口，与张辽为前锋，行遇霖雨，大军先及，水遂长，贼船稍进，将士皆不安。

translations.literal: Ba followed in campaigning against Sun Quan at Ruxukou, with Zhang Liao as vanguard; marching they encountered steady rain; the great army arrived first, the water thereupon rose, the enemy ships gradually advanced, and officers and troops were all uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: At Ruxu with Zhang Liao as vanguard, steady rain swelled the waters, enemy ships closed in, and the troops grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 辽欲去，霸止之曰：“公明於利钝，宁肯捐吾等邪？

translations.literal: Liao wished to withdraw; Ba stopped him and said: "The lord is clear on what is sharp and what is blunt—would he be willing to abandon us?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao meant to pull back; Zang Ba said Cao Cao understood the odds and would not abandon them.

sentences.zh: ”明日果有令。

translations.literal: The next day indeed there was an order.
translations.idiomatic: Orders arrived the next day as Zang Ba had predicted.

sentences.zh: 辽至，以语太祖。

translations.literal: When Liao arrived, he reported these words to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao repeated Zang Ba's words to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之，拜扬威将军，假节。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor approved, appointed him general who raises might, and lent the credential insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao approved, named him general who raises might, and gave the baton of authority.

sentences.zh: 后权乞降，太祖还，留霸与夏侯惇等屯居巢。

translations.literal: Later Quan begged to surrender; the Grand Progenitor returned, leaving Ba together with Xiahou Dun and others to garrison Juchao.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan's nominal submission Cao Cao withdrew but left Zang Ba with Xiahou Dun at Juchao.

sentences.zh: 而孙观亦至青州刺史，假节，从太祖讨孙权，战被创，薨。

translations.literal: Sun Guan also reached Inspector of Qing Province, lent the credential insignia; following the Grand Progenitor in campaigning against Sun Quan, in battle he was struck by a wound and died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Guan too became inspector of Qingzhou with the baton but died of wounds fighting Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 子毓嗣，亦至青州刺史。

translations.literal: The son Yu inherited; he also reached Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Yu inherited and also rose to inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏书》曰：孙观字仲台，泰山人。

translations.literal: The Wei shu says: Sun Guan, courtesy name Zhongtai, was a Taishan man.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei gives Sun Guan's courtesy name as Zhongtai and his origin as Taishan.

sentences.zh: 与臧霸俱起，讨黄巾，拜骑都尉。

translations.literal: Together with Zang Ba he rose, campaigned against the Yellow Turbans, and was appointed colonel of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose with Zang Ba against the Yellow Turbans and was named colonel of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太祖破吕布，使霸招观兄弟，皆厚遇之。

translations.literal: After the Grand Progenitor defeated Lü Bu, he ordered Ba to summon Guan and his brothers, and all were generously treated.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Bu fell Cao Cao had Zang Ba summon the Sun brothers and treated them generously.

sentences.zh: 与霸俱战伐，观常为先登，征定青、徐群贼，功次於霸，封吕都亭侯。

translations.literal: Together with Ba he always campaigned; Guan was always first to ascend; he campaigned to settle the Qing and Xu bandit hosts; his merit was next to Ba's; he was enfeoffed as marquis of Lü metropolitan village.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Guan was repeatedly first on the wall, his record second only to Zang Ba's, and he received a Lü village marquisate.

sentences.zh: 康亦以功封列侯。

translations.literal: Kang also by merit was enfeoffed as full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kang also earned a full marquisate for merit.

sentences.zh: 与太祖会南皮，遣子弟入居鄴，拜观偏将军，迁青州刺史。

translations.literal: Meeting the Grand Progenitor at Nanpi, he sent sons and younger brothers to dwell at Ye; Guan was appointed lieutenant general and promoted to Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanpi he sent kinsmen to Ye, was named lieutenant general, and became inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 从征孙权於濡须口，假节。

translations.literal: Following in campaigning against Sun Quan at Ruxukou, lent the credential insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He received the baton for the Ruxu campaign against Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 攻权，为流矢所中，伤左足，力战不顾，太祖劳之曰：“将军被创深重，而猛气益奋，不当为国爱身乎？

translations.literal: Attacking Quan, he was struck by a stray arrow, wounded in the left foot, yet fought hard without regard; the Grand Progenitor consoled him, saying: "The general's wound is deep and grave, yet fierce spirit grows all the more—ought you not, for the state's sake, cherish your body?"
translations.idiomatic: Wounded in the left foot by a stray shaft at Ruxu, he fought on until Cao Cao urged him to spare himself for the realm's sake.

sentences.zh: ”转振威将军，创甚，遂卒。〉

translations.literal: He was transferred to general who shakes might; the wound was very grave, and thereupon he died.〉
translations.idiomatic: The wound proved mortal, and he died soon after.〉

sentences.zh: 文聘字仲业，南阳宛人也，为刘表大将，使御北方。

translations.literal: Wen Pin, courtesy name Zhongye, was a man of Wan in Nanyang, was Liu Biao's great general, ordered to guard the north.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Pin of Wan in Nanyang was Liu Biao's senior commander on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 表死，其子琮立。

translations.literal: Biao died; his son Cong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao died, and his son Liu Cong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 太祖征荆州，琮举州降，呼聘欲与俱，聘曰：“聘不能全州，当待罪而已。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor campaigned against Jing Province; Cong raised the province in surrender; he called Pin wishing to go with him; Pin said: "Pin was unable to preserve the whole province—I await punishment, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Cong surrendered Jingzhou and summoned Wen Pin to go with him, Wen Pin refused, saying he had failed to save the province and would await punishment alone.

sentences.zh: ”太祖济汉，聘乃诣太祖，太祖问曰：“来何迟邪？

translations.literal: After the Grand Progenitor crossed the Han, Pin thereupon went to the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor asked: "Why have you come so late?"
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao crossed the Han, Wen Pin came in; Cao Cao asked why he had delayed so long.

sentences.zh: ”聘曰：“先日不能辅弼刘荆州以奉国家，荆州虽没，常原据守汉川，保全土境，生不负於孤弱，死无愧於地下，而计不得已，以至於此。

translations.literal: Pin said: "Earlier I was unable to assist Liu Jingzhou to serve the state; although Jing Province is lost, I always wished to hold the line along the Han and preserve the territory while alive not betraying the weak, while dead without shame below ground—but planning left no choice, and it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Pin said he had wished to hold the Han line for Liu Biao's heir, to live without betraying the weak and die without shame, but circumstances forced surrender.

sentences.zh: 实怀悲惭，无颜早见耳。

translations.literal: Truly I harbor grief and shame and had no face to see early."
translations.idiomatic: Shame and grief kept him from an earlier audience.

sentences.zh: ”遂欷歔流涕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sobbed and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: He wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 太祖为之怆然曰：“仲业，卿真忠臣也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor for him was moved and said: "Zhongye, you are indeed a loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was moved and called him a true loyal minister.

sentences.zh: ”厚礼待之。

translations.literal: With thick courtesy he treated him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao received him with rich honors.

sentences.zh: 授聘兵，使与曹纯追讨刘备於长阪。

translations.literal: He entrusted Pin with troops and ordered him together with Cao Chun to pursue and campaign against Liu Bei at Changban.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him troops with Cao Chun to pursue Liu Bei at Changban.

sentences.zh: 太祖先定荆州，江夏与吴接，民心不安，乃以聘为江夏太守，使典北兵，委以边事，赐爵关内侯。

translations.literal: After the Grand Progenitor first settled Jing Province, Jiangxia bordered Wu and the people's hearts were not settled, thereupon he appointed Pin governor of Jiangxia, ordered him to command northern troops, entrusted him with border affairs, and granted the noble rank of secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingzhou fell he made Wen Pin governor of Jiangxia facing Wu, gave him northern troops and the frontier, and enfeoffed him as a secondary marquis at court.

sentences.zh: 〈孙盛曰：资父事君，忠孝道一。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: Supplying a father and serving a lord, in loyal filiality the Way is one.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng observes that serving father and lord rests on the same principle of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 臧霸少有孝烈之称，文聘著垂泣之诚，是以魏武一面，委之以二方之任，岂直壮武见知於仓卒之间哉！〉

translations.literal: Zang Ba in youth had a reputation for filial fierce integrity; Wen Pin displayed the sincerity of weeping at audience—therefore on one interview King Wei of Wei entrusted them with responsibility for two regions; was it only that martial boldness was noticed in a moment of crisis!〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng argues that Zang Ba's filial repute and Wen Pin's tears won Cao Cao's trust for two borders—not mere battlefield bravado.〉

sentences.zh: 与乐进讨关羽於寻口，有功，进封延寿亭侯，加讨逆将军。

translations.literal: Together with Yue Jin he campaigned against Guan Yu at Xunkou with merit, advanced enfeoffment to marquis of the Yanshou village, and added general who chastises rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: With Yue Jin he fought Guan Yu at Xunkou, earned a larger fief at Yanshou village, and gained the title general who chastises rebellion.

sentences.zh: 又攻羽辎重於汉津，烧其船於荆城。

translations.literal: Again he attacked Yu's baggage train at Han Ford and burned his ships at Jingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Guan Yu's baggage at Han Ford and burned his boats at Jingcheng.

sentences.zh: 文帝践阼，进爵长安乡侯，假节。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, his noble rank was advanced to marquis of Chang'an village and he was lent the credential insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen raised his fief to Chang'an village and gave the baton.

sentences.zh: 与夏侯尚围江陵，使聘别屯沔口，止石梵，自当一队，御贼有功，迁后将军，封新野侯。

translations.literal: Together with Xiahou Shang besieging Jiangling, he ordered Pin separately to garrison at Hankou, stopping at Shifan, himself commanding one corps; resisting the bandits with merit, he was promoted to general of the rear and enfeoffed as marquis of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jiangling siege he held Hankou and Shifan on a separate command, distinguished himself, and became general of the rear, marquis of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 孙权以五万众自围聘於石阳，甚急，聘坚守不动，权住二十餘日乃解去。

translations.literal: Sun Quan with fifty thousand men himself besieged Pin at Shiyang; it was very urgent; Pin firmly defended without moving; Quan stayed more than twenty days and then broke off and left.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan invested him at Shiyang with fifty thousand men for over twenty days without taking the city.

sentences.zh: 聘追击破之。

translations.literal: Pin pursued, struck, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Pin counterattacked in pursuit and routed him.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：孙权尝自将数万众卒至。

translations.literal: The Wei lüe says: Sun Quan once personally led several tens of thousands of troops to arrive suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe records a surprise attack by Sun Quan with tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 时大雨，城栅崩坏，人民散在田野，未及补治。

translations.literal: At that time great rain; the city stockade collapsed; the people scattered in the fields and had not yet repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain had ruined the walls and scattered the populace before repairs.

sentences.zh: 聘闻权到，不知所施，乃思惟莫若潜默可以疑之。

translations.literal: Pin hearing Quan had arrived did not know what to do; he therefore thought nothing was better than deep silence to make them suspect.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Pin chose total stillness to make Sun Quan suspect a trap.

sentences.zh: 乃敕城中人使不得见，又自卧舍中不起。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the people in the city not to be seen, and himself lay in his quarters and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He hid the garrison from sight and stayed abed himself.

sentences.zh: 权果疑之，语其部党曰：“北方以此人忠臣也，故委之以此郡，今我至而不动，此不有密图，必当有外救。

translations.literal: Quan indeed suspected; speaking to his faction he said: "The north holds this man a loyal minister, therefore entrusts him with this commandery; now I have arrived and he does not move—either he has a secret plan or there must be outside relief."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan concluded that stillness meant ambush or reinforcements.

sentences.zh: ”遂不敢攻而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not dare attack and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew without assaulting the walls.

sentences.zh: 魏略此语，与本传反。〉

translations.literal: This language of the Wei lüe contradicts the main biography.〉
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes this anecdote contradicts the main biography.〉

sentences.zh: 增邑五百户，并前千九百户。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by five hundred households; together with the previous it was one thousand nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred more households were added for nineteen hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 聘在江夏数十年，有威恩，名震敌国，贼不敢侵。

translations.literal: Pin was in Jiangxia for several decades, had awe and grace, his name shook the enemy state, and bandits did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: For decades at Jiangxia he combined severity with kindness and kept enemies from raiding.

sentences.zh: 分聘户邑封聘子岱为列侯，又赐聘从子厚爵关内侯。

translations.literal: He divided Pin's households and enfeoffed Pin's son Dai as full marquis, and again granted Pin's nephew Hou a secondary marquisate within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The court split his fief to enfeoff Wen Dai and ennobled a nephew as secondary marquis.

sentences.zh: 聘薨，谥曰壮侯。

translations.literal: Pin died; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Pin died and was posthumously titled Marquis Zhuang, the Stalwart.

sentences.zh: 岱又先亡，聘养子休嗣。

translations.literal: Dai also died first; Pin's adopted son Xiu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Dai died before him; adopted son Wen Xiu inherited.

sentences.zh: 卒，子武嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, the son Wu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Xiu died, his son Wen Wu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 嘉平中，谯郡桓禺为江夏太守，清俭有威惠，名亚於聘。

translations.literal: In the Jiaping years, Huan Yu of Qiao commandery was governor of Jiang County, clear and frugal, with awe and kindness; his name was next to Pin's.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiaping era Huan Yu of Qiao governed Jiangxia with similar austerity and renown, second only to Wen Pin.

sentences.zh: 吕虔字子恪，任城人也。

translations.literal: Lü Qian, courtesy name Zike, was a man of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Qian, courtesy name Zike, was a native of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖在兗州，闻虔有胆策，以为从事，将家兵守湖陆。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor was in Yan Province, hearing Qian had courage and stratagems, he made him aide and led household troops to guard Hulü.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao held Yanzhou he heard of Lü Qian's courage and judgment, named him an aide, and posted his household guard at Hulü.

sentences.zh: 〔襄贲〕校尉杜松部民炅母等作乱，与昌豨通。

translations.literal: The Xiangben commandant Du Song's dependent Jiong Mu and others stirred up disorder and communicated with Chang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Du Song of Xiangben had a follower named Jiong Mu who rebelled in league with Chang Xi.

sentences.zh: 太祖以虔代松。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor made Qian replace Song.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replaced Du Song with Lü Qian.

sentences.zh: 虔到，招诱炅母渠率及同恶数十人，赐酒食。

translations.literal: When Qian arrived, he summoned and enticed Jiong Mu's chiefs and those of the same wickedness, several tens of men, and bestowed wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: He invited the ringleaders and their confederates to a feast.

sentences.zh: 简壮士伏其侧，虔察炅母等皆醉，使伏兵尽格杀之。

translations.literal: He selected stalwart soldiers concealed at their side; Qian watched until Jiong Mu and the others were all drunk, then ordered ambush troops to strike and kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: When they were drunk, hidden soldiers cut them down.

sentences.zh: 抚其餘众，群贼乃平。

translations.literal: He soothed the remaining multitude; the bandit hosts were then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the remainder and the hills grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 太祖以虔领泰山太守。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor made Qian acting governor of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao made him acting governor of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 郡接山海，世乱，闻民人多藏窜。

translations.literal: The commandery adjoins mountains and sea; in generations of chaos it was heard that very many of the people hid and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery borders mountains and sea; in the turmoil many people had fled to hiding.

sentences.zh: 袁绍所置中郎将郭祖、公孙犊等数十辈，保山为寇，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Several tens of parties such as Zhonglang generals Guo Zu and Gongsun Du whom Yuan Shao had appointed held the mountains as bandits and the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of bands led by Yuan Shao's appointees such as Guo Zu and Gongsun Du raided from the heights and oppressed the people.

sentences.zh: 虔将家兵到郡，开恩信，祖等党属皆降服，诸山中亡匿者尽出安土业。

translations.literal: Qian leading household troops came to the commandery, opened grace and trust, and Zu and company's followers all surrendered and submitted; those who had fled and hidden in the various mountains all came out and settled to their land and occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Qian brought his household guard, offered amnesty and good faith, won the surrender of the chiefs, and coaxed every refugee back to field and hearth.

sentences.zh: 简其强者补战士，泰山由是遂有精兵，冠名州郡。

translations.literal: He selected the strong among them to fill the ranks of fighters; Taishan thereupon had crack troops whose fame crowned the province.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the sturliest men into the army until Taishan fielded a corps whose name outshone neighboring commands.

sentences.zh: 济南黄巾徐和等，所在劫长吏，攻城邑。

translations.literal: The Jinan Yellow Turbans Xu He and others everywhere plundered senior clerks and attacked cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Xu He and other Jinan Yellow Turbans seized magistrates and stormed towns across the region.

sentences.zh: 虔引兵与夏侯渊会击之，前后数十战，斩首获生数千人。

translations.literal: Qian led troops to join Xiahou Yuan in striking them; before and after there were several tens of battles; beheaded heads and captured alive several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Qian joined Xiahou Yuan in dozens of actions that took thousands of heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 太祖使督青州诸郡兵以讨东莱群贼李条等，有功。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered him to supervise the troops of the various commanderies of Qing Province to campaign against the Donglai bandit hosts of Li Tiao and others; he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao put him over Qingzhou forces against the Donglai bands led by Li Tiao and won further distinction.

sentences.zh: 太祖令曰：“夫有其志，必成其事，盖烈士之所徇也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered, saying: "When one has that will, one is sure to complete the affair—that is what a man of ardor stakes himself on.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wrote, "Where the will is set, the deed follows—that is the mark of a resolute man.

sentences.zh: 卿在郡以来，禽奸讨暴，百姓获安，躬蹈矢石，所征辄克。

translations.literal: Since you came to the commandery you have seized villains and campaigned against violence; the hundred surnames have obtained peace; you yourself tread among arrows and stone; wherever you have campaigned you have prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Since you took office you have rooted out crime, fought down violence, and kept the people safe, yourself braving missile fire and winning every campaign you lead.

sentences.zh: 昔寇恂立名於汝、颍，耿弇建策於青、兗，古今一也。

translations.literal: Formerly Kou Xun established his name at Ru and Ying; Geng Yan set his plans at Qing and Yan—ancient and modern are one."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Xun won his fame between the Ru and the Ying; Geng Yan laid his plans in Qing and Yan—the same spirit links past to present."

sentences.zh: ”举茂才，加骑都尉，典郡如故。

translations.literal: He was raised as flourishing talent, added colonel of cavalry, and governed the commandery as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as flourishing talent, given the added rank of colonel of cavalry, and kept the governorship.

sentences.zh: 虔在泰山十数年，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: Qian was at Taishan for more than ten years and had great awe and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a decade at Taishan he ruled with a mix of severity and mercy that won wide respect.

sentences.zh: 许褚字仲康，谯国谯人也。

translations.literal: Xu Chu, courtesy name Zhongkang, was a man of Qiao in the princedom of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chu, courtesy name Zhongkang, came from Qiao in the princedom of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 长八尺餘，腰大十围，容貌雄毅，勇力绝人。

translations.literal: He stood more than eight chi tall, his waist measured ten girths, his bearing was fierce and stern, and his courage and strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: He stood over eight feet tall, with a massive girth, a fierce bearing, and strength beyond any ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 汉末，聚少年及宗族数千家，共坚壁以御寇。

translations.literal: At the end of Han he gathered youths and clansmen of several thousand households and jointly fortified a stockade to resist bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Han he rallied young clansmen by the thousand and threw up a walled camp against raiders.

sentences.zh: 时汝南葛陂贼万餘人攻褚壁，褚众少不敌，力战疲极。

translations.literal: At that time more than ten thousand Gebei bandits of Runan attacked Chu's stockade; Chu's multitude was few and could not match them; they fought until utterly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When ten thousand bandits from Gebei in Runan stormed his fort, Xu Chu was badly outnumbered and fought until his men were spent.

sentences.zh: 兵矢尽，乃令壁中男女，聚治石如杅斗者置四隅。

translations.literal: Arrows and bolts were exhausted; thereupon he ordered the men and women inside the stockade to gather stones shaped like pestles and mortars and set them at the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: When missiles ran out he had the defenders stack stone missiles shaped like mortars at each corner of the rampart.

sentences.zh: 褚飞石掷之，所值皆摧碎。

translations.literal: Chu hurled the flying stones; whatever they hit was shattered.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chu hurled those stones and shattered everything they struck.

sentences.zh: 贼不敢进。

translations.literal: The bandits did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders dared not close in.

sentences.zh: 粮乏，伪与贼和，以牛与贼易食，贼来取牛，牛辄奔还。

translations.literal: Food ran short; he feigned peace with the bandits and traded cattle to them for grain; when the bandits came to take the cattle, the cattle always ran back.
translations.idiomatic: Short of grain, he pretended to parley and traded cattle for food; when the enemy came to drive the cattle off, the beasts bolted home.

sentences.zh: 褚乃出陈前，一手逆曳牛尾，行百餘步。

translations.literal: Chu thereupon came out in front of the formation, with one hand seized the ox by the tail dragging backward, and walked more than a hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: He then strode before the lines, seized an ox by the tail with one hand, and dragged the beast backward more than a hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 贼众惊，遂不敢取牛而走。

translations.literal: The bandit host was amazed and thereupon did not dare take the cattle but fled.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fled in terror and abandoned the cattle.

sentences.zh: 由是淮、汝、陈、梁间，闻皆畏惮之。

translations.literal: Thereby between the Huai, Ru, Chen, and Liang all who heard were in awe and fear of him.
translations.idiomatic: From the Huai to the Ru and across Chen and Liang, every bandit who heard his name was afraid.

sentences.zh: 太祖徇淮、汝，褚以众归太祖。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned along the Huai and Ru, Chu with his multitude submitted to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao campaigned along the Huai and Ru, Xu Chu brought his followers over.

sentences.zh: 太祖见而壮之曰：“此吾樊哙也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor saw him and thought him brave, saying: "This is my Fan Kuai."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took one look and said, "Here is my Fan Kuai."

sentences.zh: ”即日拜都尉，引入宿卫。

translations.literal: The same day he was appointed commandant and brought in to serve in the night guard.
translations.idiomatic: That day he was named commandant of the guard and taken into the night watch.

sentences.zh: 诸从褚侠客，皆以为虎士。

translations.literal: All the knight-errants who followed Chu were made tiger warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Every fighting man who had followed Xu Chu was enrolled as a tiger warrior.

sentences.zh: 从征张绣，先登，斩首万计，迁校尉。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Zhang Xiu, was first to ascend, and beheaded heads numbering in the tens of thousands; he was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He spearheaded the campaign against Zhang Xiu, took uncounted heads, and rose to colonel.

sentences.zh: 从讨袁绍於官渡。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Yuan Shao at Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Yuan Shao at Guandu.

sentences.zh: 时常从士徐他等谋为逆，以褚常侍左右，惮之不敢发。

translations.literal: At that time attendants such as Xu Ta plotted treason, but because Chu always attended at the left and right, they feared him and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants led by Xu Ta plotted assassination, but Xu Chu never left Cao Cao's side and they dared not strike.

sentences.zh: 伺褚休下日，他等怀刀入。

translations.literal: They waited for the day Chu was off duty below; Ta and the others hid knives and entered.
translations.idiomatic: They chose a day when Xu Chu was off duty and slipped in with concealed blades.

sentences.zh: 褚至下舍心动，即还侍。

translations.literal: When Chu reached his lower quarters his heart stirred; he immediately returned to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chu felt a premonition at his quarters and hurried back to the tent.

sentences.zh: 他等不知，入帐见褚，大惊愕。

translations.literal: Ta and the others did not know; entering the tent they saw Chu and were greatly startled.
translations.idiomatic: The assassins entered the tent unaware and froze when they saw him.

sentences.zh: 他色变，褚觉之，即击杀他等。

translations.literal: Ta's color changed; Chu perceived it and immediately struck and killed Ta and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ta blanched; Xu Chu killed him and his accomplices on the spot.

sentences.zh: 太祖益亲信之，出入同行，不离左右。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor all the more trusted him intimately; going out and entering they went together and he did not leave the left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao trusted him utterly and kept him at his shoulder day and night.

sentences.zh: 从围鄴，力战有功，赐爵关内侯。

translations.literal: He followed in besieging Ye, fought hard with merit, and was granted the noble rank of secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Ye he fought with distinction and received a secondary marquisate at court.

sentences.zh: 从讨韩遂、马超於潼关。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Han Sui and Ma Chao at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Tong Pass campaign against Han Sui and Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 太祖将北渡，临济河，先渡兵，独与褚及虎士百餘人留南岸断后。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was about to cross north; coming to the Ji River he first crossed the troops, and alone with Chu and more than a hundred tiger warriors remained on the south bank to cover the rear.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ji River Cao Cao sent the army across first while he stayed on the south bank with Xu Chu and a hundred tiger warriors as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 超将步骑万餘人，来奔太祖军，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: Chao led more than ten thousand foot and horse who came charging at the Grand Progenitor's army; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao charged with over ten thousand horse and foot while arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 褚白太祖，贼来多，今兵渡已尽，宜去，乃扶太祖上船。

translations.literal: Chu reported to the Grand Progenitor: "The bandits come in great numbers; the men who have crossed are all on the north shore—we must board at once." Thereupon he helped the Grand Progenitor onto a boat.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chu saw Ma Chao's massed charge and warned that everyone who could cross had already crossed; they had to embark immediately, and he helped Cao Cao onto the boat.

sentences.zh: 贼战急，军争济，船重欲没。

translations.literal: The bandits pressed the fight urgently; the army scrambled to cross; the boat was heavy and about to sink.
translations.idiomatic: The fight grew desperate; men mobbed the boats until the hulls nearly swamped.

sentences.zh: 褚斩攀船者，左手举马鞍蔽太祖。

translations.literal: Chu struck those who clambered on the boat; with his left hand he raised a saddle to shield the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chu cut down men who overloaded the boat, raised a saddle with his left arm to shield Cao Cao,

sentences.zh: 船工为流矢所中死，褚右手并溯船，仅乃得渡。

translations.literal: The boatman was struck by a stray arrow and died; Chu with his right hand also pulled the boat upstream, and barely crossed.
translations.idiomatic: and when the ferryman fell dead to a stray shaft he sculled the boat one-handed until they reached the far bank.

sentences.zh: 是日，微褚几危。

translations.literal: That day, had it not been for Chu, it would nearly have been perilous.
translations.idiomatic: That day Cao Cao would almost certainly have perished but for Xu Chu.

sentences.zh: 其后太祖与遂、超等单马会语，左右皆不得从，唯将褚。

translations.literal: Afterward the Grand Progenitor with Sui, Chao, and others met on single horses to talk; those at left and right were not permitted to follow; he led only Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cao Cao met Han Sui and Ma Chao with no escort except Xu Chu.

sentences.zh: 超负其力，阴欲前突太祖，素闻褚勇，疑从骑是褚。

translations.literal: Chao trusted in his strength and secretly wished to charge forward and strike the Grand Progenitor; always hearing of Chu's courage, he suspected the mounted follower was Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao meant to use his prowess to rush Cao Cao but feared the lone rider might be Xu Chu.

sentences.zh: 乃问太祖曰：“公有虎侯者安在？

translations.literal: Thereupon he asked the Grand Progenitor: "Where is the lord's Tiger Marquis?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked where Cao Cao's "Tiger Marquis" was.

sentences.zh: ”太祖顾指褚，褚瞋目盼之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor turned his glance and pointed to Chu; Chu glared with bulging eyes at him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pointed at Xu Chu, who glared back at Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 超不敢动，乃各罢。

translations.literal: Chao did not dare move, and thereupon each broke off.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao dared not move, and the parley ended.

sentences.zh: 后数日会战，大破超等，褚身斩首级，迁武卫中郎将。

translations.literal: Several days later they joined battle; they greatly defeated Chao and the others; Chu personally beheaded enemy heads and was promoted to general of the household guard of martial might.
translations.idiomatic: In the general engagement days later Xu Chu killed with his own hand and was promoted to general of the household guard of martial might.

sentences.zh: 武卫之号，自此始也。

translations.literal: The title guard of martial might began from this.
translations.idiomatic: That was the origin of the "martial guard" title.

sentences.zh: 军中以褚力如虎而痴，故号曰虎痴；

translations.literal: In the army, because Chu's strength was like a tiger yet he was simple-minded, they therefore styled him Tiger Simpleton;
translations.idiomatic: The troops called him the tiger simpleton for his brute strength and blunt manner;

sentences.zh: 是以超问虎侯，至今天下称焉，皆谓其姓名也。

translations.literal: therefore when Chao asked of the Tiger Marquis, to this day the realm styles him so—all refer to his name and person.
translations.idiomatic: so when Ma Chao asked after the Tiger Marquis, the nickname stuck and the world still uses it for Xu Chu himself.

sentences.zh: 典韦，陈留己吾人也。

translations.literal: Dian Wei was a man of Jiwu in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Dian Wei came from Jiwu in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 形貌魁梧，旅力过人，有志节任侠。

translations.literal: His form and bearing were towering; his strength on the march surpassed others; he had resolve and integrity and acted the knight-errant.
translations.idiomatic: He was huge of frame, enormously strong, high-minded, and a sworn champion of justice.

sentences.zh: 襄邑刘氏与睢阳李永为雠，韦为报之。

translations.literal: The Liu clan of Xiangyi and Li Yong of Suiyang were enemies; Wei avenged them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu family of Xiangyi feuded with Li Yong of Suiyang, and Dian Wei undertook to settle the score.

sentences.zh: 永故富春长，备卫甚谨。

translations.literal: Yong had formerly been magistrate of Fuchun; his preparations and guards were very strict.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong had once been magistrate of Fuchun and kept a tight guard about himself.

sentences.zh: 韦乘车载鸡酒，伪为候者，门开，怀匕首入杀永，并杀其妻，徐出，取车上刀戟，步

translations.literal: Wei rode in a cart loaded with chickens and wine, pretending to be a caller; when the gate opened he, hiding a dagger in his robe, entered, killed Yong, and also killed his wife; leisurely he came out, took from the cart halberd and spear, and walked
translations.idiomatic: He drove up with fowl and wine like a petitioner, slipped a dagger inside his robe when the gate opened, killed Li Yong and his wife, then stepped out, armed himself from the cart, and walked away

translations.literal: (chu) — marginal gloss on the verb of exit.
translations.idiomatic: An editorial note glosses the verb for exiting.
He completed his withdrawal from the compound.

sentences.zh: 永居近巿，一巿尽骇。

translations.literal: Yong's dwelling was near the market; the whole market was terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong lived beside the market; panic swept the stalls.

sentences.zh: 追者数百，莫敢近。

translations.literal: Several hundred pursuers followed, yet none dared approach.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds gave chase but none dared close with him.

sentences.zh: 行四五里，遇其伴，转战得脱。

translations.literal: Going four or five li he met his companions, fought in rotation, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: After four or five li he met his confederates, fought a running skirmish, and broke clear.

sentences.zh: 由是为豪杰所识。

translations.literal: Thereby he was noticed by the bold spirits of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting men of the region took note of his name.

sentences.zh: 初平中，张邈举义兵，韦为士，属司马赵宠。

translations.literal: In the Chuping years Zhang Miao raised righteous troops; Wei was a soldier, subordinate to Major Zhao Chong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chuping era Zhang Miao raised loyal troops; Dian Wei served as a soldier under Major Zhao Chong.

sentences.zh: 牙门旗长大，人莫能胜，韦一手建之，宠异其才力。

translations.literal: The gate camp banner was long and great; no man could raise it; Wei with one hand set it up; Chong marveled at his talent and strength.
translations.idiomatic: The camp gate banner was too heavy for any man to raise until Dian Wei lifted it one-handed; Zhao Chong marveled at his strength.

sentences.zh: 后属夏侯惇，数斩首有功，拜司马。

translations.literal: Later he was subordinate to Xiahou Dun, repeatedly beheaded heads with merit, and was appointed major.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Xiahou Dun, piled up beheadings, and became a major.

sentences.zh: 太祖讨吕布於濮阳。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor campaigned against Lü Bu at Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao attacked Lü Bu at Puyang.

sentences.zh: 布有别屯在濮阳西四五十里，太祖夜袭，比明破之。

translations.literal: Bu had a separate encampment forty or fifty li west of Puyang; the Grand Progenitor raided it by night and by dawn had broken it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu held an outpost west of Puyang; Cao Cao stormed it by night and took it by dawn.

sentences.zh: 未及还，会布救兵至，三面掉战。

translations.literal: Before he could return, Bu's relief troops arrived and pressed battle on three sides.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could withdraw, Lü Bu's reinforcements arrived and pressed him on three sides.

sentences.zh: 时布身自搏战，自旦至日昳数十合，相持急。

translations.literal: At that time Bu himself joined close combat; from dawn past noon there were several tens of clashes; the standoff was urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu fought in person from dawn past noon in dozens of rounds without a break.

sentences.zh: 太祖募陷陈，韦先占，将应募者数十人，皆重衣两铠，弃楯，但持长矛撩戟。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor recruited men to break the formation; Wei was first to volunteer and led several tens who answered the call; all wore double armor and heavy coats, discarded shields, and bore only long spears and halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao called for volunteers to break the enemy line; Dian Wei led dozens in double armor, no shields, only long spears and halberds.

sentences.zh: 时西面又急，韦进当之，贼弓弩乱发，矢至如雨，韦不视，谓等人曰：“虏来十步，乃白之。

translations.literal: At that time the west face was again urgent; Wei advanced to meet it; the enemy crossbows shot wildly; arrows arrived like rain; Wei did not look and said to his companions: "When the bandits are ten paces, then tell me."
translations.idiomatic: The western sector buckled; Dian Wei advanced into a storm of bolts and told his men to warn him at ten paces.

sentences.zh: ”等人曰：“十步矣。

translations.literal: The companions said: "Ten paces."
translations.idiomatic: They cried, "Ten paces!"

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“五步乃白。

translations.literal: Again he said: "At five paces tell me."
translations.idiomatic: "Tell me at five," he said.

sentences.zh: ”等人惧，疾言“虏至矣”！

translations.literal: The companions were afraid and urgently said: "The bandits have arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: Panicked, they shouted that the enemy was on him.

sentences.zh: 韦手持十餘戟，大呼起，所抵无不应手倒者。

translations.literal: Chu held more than ten halberds, gave a great shout and rose; none whom he met did not fall at the stroke of his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Dian Wei gripped a sheaf of halberds, roared, and charged; every foe before him dropped.

sentences.zh: 布众退。

translations.literal: Bu's multitude withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's men fell back.

sentences.zh: 会日暮，太祖乃得引去。

translations.literal: It happened to be dusk; the Grand Progenitor was thereupon able to lead away.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Cao Cao was able to break off.

sentences.zh: 拜韦都尉，引置左右，将亲兵数百人，常绕大帐。

translations.literal: Wei was appointed commandant, brought in to attend at the left and right, and led several hundred personal troops who constantly circled the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: Dian Wei was named commandant, given several hundred bodyguards, and stationed them around the headquarters tent.

sentences.zh: 韦既壮武，其所将皆选卒，每战斗，常先登陷陈。

translations.literal: Wei was both mighty and martial; those he led were all picked soldiers; in every battle he was always first to ascend and break the formation.
