translations.idiomatic: A fearsome fighter, he led picked troops and was always first through the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 迁为校尉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to colonel.

sentences.zh: 性忠至谨重，常昼立侍终日，夜宿帐左右，稀归私寝。

translations.literal: By nature he was loyal to the utmost, careful and weighty; he often stood attending all day in daylight and by night slept to the left and right of the tent, seldom returning to private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast and vigilant, he stood guard all day and slept beside the headquarters tent by night, rarely visiting his own quarters.

sentences.zh: 好酒食，饮啖兼人，每赐食於前，大饮长歠，左右相属，数人益乃供，太祖壮之。

translations.literal: He loved wine and food; eating and drinking surpassed other men; whenever feasts were bestowed before him he drank deep and long draughts; those to left and right followed one after another; only when several men more were added was supply enough; the Grand Progenitor thought him brave.
translations.idiomatic: He ate and drank for several men at every feast Cao Cao gave, and Cao Cao admired his appetite as part of his valor.

sentences.zh: 韦好持大双戟与长刀等，军中为之语曰：“帐下壮士有典君，提一双戟八十斤。

translations.literal: Wei liked to carry great paired halberds and a long blade as long as others; the army made a rhyme of him: "Under the tent the stalwart has Lord Dian; he lifts a pair of halberds of eighty jin."
translations.idiomatic: The troops sang of him: "Under the tent stands Dian Wei, hefting twin halberds of eighty jin."

translations.literal: Closing line of the soldiers' rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: That was the tag line of the soldiers' song about him.

sentences.zh: 太祖征荆州，至宛，张绣迎降。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor campaigned against Jing Province; reaching Wan, Zhang Xiu came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jingzhou expedition Cao Cao reached Wan, where Zhang Xiu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚悦，延绣及其将帅，置酒高会。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was very pleased, extended Xiu and his generals, and set out wine for a high feast.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao feasted Zhang Xiu and his officers in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 太祖行酒，韦持大斧立后，刃径尺，太祖所至之前，韦辄举斧目之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor went round pouring wine; Wei held a great axe standing behind; the blade was a foot across; wherever the Grand Progenitor went before, Wei always raised the axe and glared.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao poured the wine while Dian Wei stood behind him with a broad-bladed axe, glaring at each guest Cao Cao approached.

sentences.zh: 竟酒，绣及其将帅莫敢仰视。

translations.literal: When the wine ended, Xiu and his generals none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet ended Zhang Xiu and his officers dared not lift their eyes.

sentences.zh: 后十餘日，绣反，袭太祖营，太祖出战不利，轻骑引去。

translations.literal: After more than ten days Xiu rebelled, raided the Grand Progenitor's camp; the Grand Progenitor went out to fight with unfavorable outcome and led away with light horse.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Zhang Xiu mutinied, struck the camp, and Cao Cao fled on light horse after a reverse.

sentences.zh: 韦战於门中，贼不得入。

translations.literal: Wei fought in the gate so the bandits could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Dian Wei held the gate so the enemy could not force it.

sentences.zh: 兵遂散从他门并入。

translations.literal: The troops thereupon scattered and entered from another gate together.
translations.idiomatic: The attackers poured in through another gate.

sentences.zh: 时韦校尚有十餘人，皆殊死战，无不一当十。

translations.literal: At that time Wei's camp still had more than ten men; all fought to the death; none failed to match ten.
translations.idiomatic: A dozen of his men fought to the last, each worth ten ordinary soldiers.

sentences.zh: 贼前后至稍多，韦以长戟左右击之，一叉入，辄十餘矛摧。

translations.literal: The bandits arrived front and rear in gradually greater numbers; Wei with the long halberd struck left and right; one thrust went in and always more than ten spears were broken.
translations.idiomatic: As the press thickened he swung his long halberd until spears snapped by the dozen at each blow.

sentences.zh: 左右死伤者略尽。

translations.literal: Those at left and right were dead or wounded almost to the last.
translations.idiomatic: His followers fell until almost none were left.

sentences.zh: 韦被数十创，短兵接战，贼前搏之。

translations.literal: Wei received several tens of wounds, joined battle with short weapons, and the bandits closed to grapple him.
translations.idiomatic: Riddled with wounds, he closed to knife range as the enemy tried to seize him.

sentences.zh: 韦双挟两贼击杀之，餘贼不敢前。

translations.literal: Wei with both arms seized two bandits, killed them with a crush, and the remaining bandits did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: He seized two assailants, crushed them dead, and the rest hung back.

sentences.zh: 韦复前突贼，杀数人，创重发，瞋目大骂而死。

translations.literal: Wei again charged forward into the bandits, killed several men; his wounds reopened severely; glaring with eyes he reviled and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lunged again, cut down more men, then collapsed as his wounds reopened, glaring and cursing as he died.

sentences.zh: 贼乃敢前，取其头，传观之，覆军就视其躯。

translations.literal: The bandits then dared advance; they took his head, passed it around to view, and covered the army to come look on his trunk.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did they take his head, pass it among the ranks, and crowd around his body.

sentences.zh: 太祖退住舞阴，闻韦死，为流涕，募间取其丧，亲自临哭之，遣归葬襄邑，拜子满为郎中。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor withdrew and halted at Wuyin; hearing Wei had died, he wept for him, offered a reward to secretly recover the corpse, personally came to weep over him, sent him back for burial at Xiangyi, and appointed his son Man gentleman of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao halted at Wuyin, wept for Dian Wei, ransomed his body for burial at Xiangyi, and appointed his son Dian Man as a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 车驾每过，常祠以中牢。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial carriages passed, he always sacrificed to him with the middle victim.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the imperial train passed the site, Cao Cao sacrificed to him with an ox and a sheep.

sentences.zh: 太祖思韦，拜满为司马，引自近。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor missed Wei, appointed Man major, and brought him near.
translations.idiomatic: Missing Dian Wei, Cao Cao made Dian Man a major and kept him close at hand.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，以满为都尉，赐爵关内侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the kingly throne, he appointed Man commandant and granted the noble rank of secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the kingship he named Dian Man commandant of the guard and enfeoffed him as a secondary marquis at court.

sentences.zh: 庞德字令明，南安狟道人也。

translations.literal: Pang De, courtesy name Lingming, was a man of Yuandao in Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Pang De, courtesy name Lingming, came from Yuandao district in Nan'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈狟音桓。〉

translations.literal: The character in the place name is glossed with the reading huan.
translations.idiomatic: The place name is read with the sound huan, as noted in the margin.

sentences.zh: 少为郡吏州从事。

translations.literal: In youth he was a commandery clerk and provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a commandery clerk and provincial staff officer.

sentences.zh: 初平中，从马腾击反羌叛氐。

translations.literal: In the Chuping years he followed Ma Teng in attacking rebellious Qiang and traitorous Di.
translations.idiomatic: During Chuping he campaigned with Ma Teng against rebel Qiang and Di tribes.

sentences.zh: 数有功，稍迁至校尉。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he had merit and was gradually promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He won repeated distinction and rose to colonel.

sentences.zh: 建安中，太祖讨袁谭、尚於黎阳，谭遣郭援、高幹等略取河东，太祖使锺繇率关中诸将讨之。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an years the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Yuan Tan and Shang at Liyang; Tan dispatched Guo Yuan, Gao Gan, and others to raid Hedong; the Grand Progenitor ordered Zhong Yao to lead the Guanzhong generals against them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an Cao Cao fought Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang at Liyang; Yuan Tan sent Guo Yuan and Gao Gan into Hedong, and Cao Cao sent Zhong Yao with the Liangzhou generals to answer them.

sentences.zh: 德随腾子超拒援、幹於平阳，德为军锋，进攻援、幹，大破之，亲斩援首。

translations.literal: De followed Teng's son Chao to resist Yuan and Gan at Pingyang; De was army vanguard, advanced to attack Yuan and Gan, greatly defeated them, and personally beheaded Yuan's head.
translations.idiomatic: Pang De served under Ma Chao at Pingyang against Guo Yuan and Gao Gan, spearheaded the attack, shattered them, and cut off Guo Yuan's head himself.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：德手斩一级，不知是援。

translations.literal: The Wei lüe says: De with his own hand cut off one head and did not know it was Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe adds that Pang De took a head in the melée without knowing it was Guo Yuan.

sentences.zh: 战罢之后，众人皆言援死而不得其首。

translations.literal: After the battle ended, everyone said Yuan was dead but his head could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle everyone knew Guo Yuan was dead but no one could find the head.

sentences.zh: 援，锺繇之甥。

translations.literal: Yuan was Zhong Yao's sister's son.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan was Zhong Yao's nephew.

sentences.zh: 德晚后於鞬中出一头，繇见之而哭。

translations.literal: De afterward brought out a head from his quiver; Yao saw it and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Pang De later produced the head from his saddle quiver; Zhong Yao wept at the sight.

sentences.zh: 德谢繇，繇曰：“援虽我甥，乃国贼也。

translations.literal: De apologized to Yao; Yao said: "Although Yuan was my sister's son, he was a traitor to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Pang De apologized, but Zhong Yao said Guo Yuan had been a rebel despite the family tie.

sentences.zh: 卿何谢之？

translations.literal: Why do you apologize?"
translations.idiomatic: There was nothing to apologize for."
End of the Wei lüe quotation.〉

sentences.zh: 拜中郎将，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed general of the household and enfeoffed as marquis of the metropolitan village.
translations.idiomatic: He was named a general of the household and received a village marquisate at the capital.

sentences.zh: 后张白骑叛於弘农，德复随腾征之，破白骑於两殽间。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Baiqi rebelled in Hongnong; De again followed Teng to campaign against him and defeated Baiqi between the two Xiao gorges.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Baiqi revolted in Hongnong, Pang De again followed Ma Teng and crushed him between the two Xiao passes.

sentences.zh: 每战，常陷陈卻敌，勇冠腾军。

translations.literal: In every battle he always broke formations and repelled the enemy; his courage crowned Teng's army.
translations.idiomatic: In every fight he shattered enemy lines and ranked first in courage in Ma Teng's host.

sentences.zh: 后腾徵为卫尉，德留属超。

translations.literal: Later Teng was summoned to be Minister of the Guards; De remained and was attached to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Teng was called to the capital as minister of the guards, Pang De stayed with Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 太祖破超於渭南，德随超亡入汉阳，保冀城。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor defeated Chao south of the Wei; De followed Chao fleeing into Hanyang and held Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao defeated Ma Chao south of the Wei, Pang De fled with him into Hanyang and held Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 后复随超奔汉中，从张鲁。

translations.literal: Later again he followed Chao fleeing to Hanzhong and joined Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Ma Chao to Hanzhong and submitted to Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 太祖定汉中，德随众降。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified Hanzhong, De followed the multitude in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao took Hanzhong, Pang De surrendered with the rest.

sentences.zh: 太祖素闻其骁勇，拜立义将军，封关门亭侯，邑三百户。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor had long heard of his fierce courage, appointed him general who establishes righteousness, enfeoffed him as marquis of the Guanmen village, and granted three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, knowing his reputation, named him general who establishes righteousness, enfeoffed him at Guanmen village with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 侯音、卫开等以宛叛，德将所领与曹仁共攻拔宛，斩音、开，遂南屯樊，讨关羽。

translations.literal: Hou Yin, Wei Kai, and others rebelled at Wan; De led those he commanded together with Cao Ren to attack and take Wan, beheaded Yin and Kai, then moved south to garrison Fan and campaigned against Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan rose under Hou Yin and Wei Kai, Pang De joined Cao Ren, took the city, executed the leaders, then marched to Fan against Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 樊下诸将以德兄在汉中，颇疑之。

translations.literal: The generals below Fan because De's elder brother was in Hanzhong were rather suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: The officers at Fan doubted him because his brother served in Hanzhong with Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：德从兄名柔，时在蜀。〉

translations.literal: The Wei lüe says: De's elder cousin was named Rou and was at that time in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe names his cousin Pang Rou as then serving in Shu.

sentences.zh: 德常曰：“我受国恩，义在效死。

translations.literal: De often said: "I have received the state's grace; righteousness lies in staking my life.
translations.idiomatic: Pang De often swore that he owed the Wei court his life.

sentences.zh: 我欲身自击羽。

translations.literal: I wish personally to strike Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to meet Guan Yu in single combat.

sentences.zh: 今年我不杀羽，羽当杀我。

translations.literal: This year if I do not kill Yu, Yu will kill me."
translations.idiomatic: Either he would kill Guan Yu this year or die in the attempt."

sentences.zh: ”后亲与羽交战，射羽中额。

translations.literal: Afterward he personally joined battle with Yu and shot Yu in the forehead.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Guan Yu in person and put a bolt in his forehead.

sentences.zh: 时德常乘白马，羽军谓之白马将军，皆惮之。

translations.literal: At that time De always rode a white horse; Yu's army called him the White Horse General and all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Riding a white horse, he was known to Guan Yu's men as the White Horse General and widely feared.

sentences.zh: 仁使德屯樊北十里，会天霖雨十餘日，汉水暴溢，樊下平地五六丈，德与诸将避水上堤。

translations.literal: Ren ordered De to garrison ten li north of Fan; it happened that heaven sent steady rain for more than ten days; the Han River rose violently; the ground below Fan was five or six zhang deep in water; De and the various generals took refuge on a dike above the water.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren posted him ten li north of Fan; weeks of rain swelled the Han until the plain was flooded; the Wei commanders clung to a levee.

sentences.zh: 羽乘船攻之，以大船四面射堤上。

translations.literal: Yu attacked them by boat, using great boats to shoot from four sides at those on the dike.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu brought warboats and raked the levee with archery from every side.

sentences.zh: 德被甲持弓，箭不虚发。

translations.literal: De donned armor and held a bow; no arrow missed its mark.
translations.idiomatic: Armored, he shot without wasting a shaft.

sentences.zh: 将军董衡、部曲将董超等欲降，德皆收斩之。

translations.literal: Generals Dong Heng and subordinate commanders Dong Chao and others wished to surrender; De seized and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Dong Heng, Dong Chao, and others who talked of surrender.

sentences.zh: 自平旦力战至日过中，羽攻益急，矢尽，短兵接战。

translations.literal: From dawn he fought hard past midday; Yu's attack grew more urgent; arrows were exhausted and they joined battle with short weapons.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn past noon the pressure grew; when shafts ran out the fight closed to knives.

sentences.zh: 德谓督将成何曰：“吾闻良将不怯死以苟免，烈士不毁节以求生，今日，我死日也。

translations.literal: De said to supervisor Cheng He: "I have heard that good generals do not fear death to seek escape, and men of ardor do not destroy their integrity to beg life—today is my day to die."
translations.idiomatic: He told Cheng He that a good general does not cling to life nor a hero break faith—this would be his day to die.

sentences.zh: ”战益怒，气愈壮，而水浸盛，吏士皆降。

translations.literal: The fighting grew more furious, his spirit more fierce, yet the water rose ever higher; clerks and soldiers all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with rising fury even as the flood rose and his men gave way around him.

sentences.zh: 德与麾下将一人，五伯二人，弯弓傅矢，乘小船欲还仁营。

translations.literal: De with one general under his command, two squad leaders, bent bows and fitted arrows, and took a small boat wishing to return to Ren's camp.
translations.idiomatic: With one officer and two sergeants he tried to row back to Cao Ren's camp.

sentences.zh: 水盛船覆，失弓矢，独抱船覆水中，为羽所得，立而不跪。

translations.literal: The water was high and the boat capsized; he lost bow and arrows; alone he embraced the overturned boat in the water and was captured by Yu; he stood and would not kneel.
translations.idiomatic: The boat swamped; unarmed in the water he was taken but refused to kneel before Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 羽谓曰：“卿兄在汉中，我欲以卿为将，不早降何为？

translations.literal: Yu said to him: "Your elder brother is in Hanzhong; I wish to employ you as a general—why not surrender early?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu offered him command, citing his brother in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: ”德骂羽曰：“竖子，何谓降也！

translations.literal: De reviled Yu, saying: "You wretch—what talk of surrender!
translations.idiomatic: Pang De cursed him as a mere upstart and scorned the word surrender.

sentences.zh: 魏王带甲百万，威振天下。

translations.literal: The King of Wei has a million armored men and awe that shakes the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wei fields a million armored soldiers and strikes terror across the realm.

sentences.zh: 汝刘备庸才耳，岂能敌邪！

translations.literal: You Liu Bei are a mediocrity—how can you resist!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was a mediocrity who could never prevail!"

sentences.zh: 我宁为国家鬼，不为贼将也。

translations.literal: I would rather be a ghost of the state than a general for bandits."
translations.idiomatic: He would rather be a loyal ghost of Wei than Guan Yu's officer."

sentences.zh: ”遂为羽所杀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was killed by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu had him executed.

sentences.zh: 太祖闻而悲之，为之流涕，封其二子为列侯。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor heard and grieved for him, shed tears for him, and enfeoffed his two sons as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wept for him and enfeoffed both sons as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，乃遣使就德墓赐谥，策曰：“昔先轸丧元，王蠋绝脰，陨身徇节，前代美之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the kingly throne, he dispatched an envoy to De's tomb to grant a posthumous title; the patent said: "Formerly Xian Zhen lost his head; Wang Zhu severed his throat; they threw away their bodies to follow integrity—the former age praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cao Pi sent an edict to Pang De's tomb, comparing him to Xian Zhen and Wang Zhu.

sentences.zh: 惟侯式昭果毅，蹈难成名，声溢当时，义高在昔，寡人愍焉，谥曰壮侯。

translations.literal: Only you, lord, made clear resolute courage, met hardship to win a name, your fame overflowed your age, your righteousness towered over the past—I pity you and grant the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang."
translations.idiomatic: The edict praised his steadfast courage and posthumously titled him Marquis Zhuang, the Stalwart."

sentences.zh: ”又赐子会等四人爵关内侯，邑各百户。

translations.literal: Again he granted his sons Hui and four others secondary marquisates within the passes, each one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons including Pang Hui received secondary marquisates of a hundred households each.

sentences.zh: 会勇烈有父风，官至中尉将军，封列侯。

translations.literal: Hui was fierce and resolute in his father's manner; his office reached general of the capital guard; he was enfeoffed as full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Hui matched his father's valor, rose to general of the capital guard, and held a full marquisate.

sentences.zh: 〈王隐《蜀记》曰：锺会平蜀，前后鼓吹，迎德尸丧还葬鄴，冢中身首如生。

translations.literal: Wang Yin's Shu ji says: When Zhong Hui pacified Shu, with front and rear drums and pipes he welcomed De's coffin back for burial at Ye; in the tomb the body and head were as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin records that Zhong Hui brought Pang De's remains to Ye for reburial with full honors.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案德死於樊城，文帝即位，又遣使至德墓所，则其尸丧不应在蜀。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi examines: De died at Fancheng; when Emperor Wen ascended the throne he again sent an envoy to De's tomb—therefore his corpse ought not to have been in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi argues Pang De died at Fan and the tale of a body in Shu is inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 此王隐之虚说也。〉

translations.literal: This is Wang Yin's empty tale.〉
translations.idiomatic: He dismisses Wang Yin's story as fiction.〉

sentences.zh: 母 趙娥

translations.literal: Mother Zhao E
translations.idiomatic: The rubric introduces Lady Zhao E, mother of Pang Jun.

sentences.zh: 初，淯外祖父赵安为同县李寿所杀，淯舅兄弟三人同时病死，寿家喜。

translations.literal: Formerly, outside the mother's family, Jun's maternal grandfather Zhao An was killed by Li Shou of the same county; Jun's maternal uncles, three brothers, simultaneously died of illness; Shou's household rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Jun's maternal grandfather Zhao An was murdered by Li Shou; when Zhao's three sons died in a plague, Li Shou's clan celebrated.

sentences.zh: 淯母娥自伤父雠不报，乃帏车袖剑，白日刺寿於都亭前，讫，徐诣县，颜色不变，曰：“父雠己报，请受戮。

translations.literal: Jun's mother E, grieving that her father's enemy went unavenged, screened a cart, hid a sword in her sleeve, and in broad daylight stabbed Shou before the metropolitan pavilion; when done, slowly she went to the county seat, her color unchanged, saying: "My father's enemy is avenged; I ask to receive execution."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhao E avenged her father by killing Li Shou at the county pavilion in daylight, then walked to the magistrate and asked to die.

sentences.zh: ”禄福长尹嘉解印绶纵娥，娥不肯去，遂强载还家。

translations.literal: The Lufu magistrate Yin Jia removed his seal-ribbons and released E; E would not leave, so he forced her into a cart and returned her home.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Yin Jia of Lufu resigned his seal rather than try her and sent her home by cart.

sentences.zh: 会赦得免，州郡叹贵，刊石表闾。

translations.literal: It happened that an amnesty arrived and she was spared; the province and commandery praised her nobility and carved a stone to mark her lane.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty spared her; the region honored her with a stone memorial at her gate.

sentences.zh: 〈皇甫谧《列女传》曰：酒泉烈女庞娥亲者，表氏庞子夏之妻，禄福赵君安之女也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi's Biographies of Women says: The fierce lady of Jiuquan Pang Eqin was the wife of the Biao clansman Pang Zixia and the daughter of Lufu Zhao Jun'an.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi's Lie nü zhuan identifies her as Pang Eqin of Jiuquan, wife of Pang Zixia and daughter of Zhao Jun'an of Lufu.

sentences.zh: 君安为同县李寿所杀，娥亲有男弟三人，皆欲报仇，寿深以为备。

translations.literal: Jun'an was killed by Li Shou of the same county; Eqin had three younger brothers who all wished to avenge him; Shou deeply took precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jun'an's murderer Li Shou was watched by three Zhao brothers who meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 会遭灾疫，三人皆死。

translations.literal: It happened that a pestilence struck and all three died.
translations.idiomatic: A plague carried off all three brothers.

sentences.zh: 寿闻大喜，请会宗族，共相庆贺，云：“赵氏强壮已尽，唯有女弱，何足复忧！

translations.literal: Shou hearing rejoiced greatly, invited his clan to a gathering, and together they celebrated, saying: "The Zhao stalwarts are all gone—only weak women remain—what need is there to worry further!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou feasted his kin, boasting that only women were left in the Zhao line.

sentences.zh: ”防备懈弛。

translations.literal: His preparations slackened.
translations.idiomatic: He relaxed his guard.

sentences.zh: 娥亲子淯出行，闻寿此言，还以启娥亲。

translations.literal: Eqin's son Jun went out and, hearing Shou's words, returned to tell Eqin.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Pang Jun heard the boast and told his mother.

sentences.zh: 娥亲既素有报仇之心，及闻寿言，感激愈深，怆然陨涕曰：“李寿，汝莫喜也，终不活汝！

translations.literal: Eqin had long harbored a heart to avenge her father; hearing Shou's words, her passion grew deeper; sadly shedding tears she said: "Li Shou, do not rejoice—you will not live!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhao swore she would not leave Li Shou alive.

sentences.zh: 戴履天地，为吾门户，吾三子之羞也。

translations.literal: I tread heaven and earth as my gate; it is the shame of my three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth were witness to the shame of her dead brothers.

sentences.zh: 焉知娥亲不手刃杀汝，而自儌倖邪？

translations.literal: How do you know Eqin will not with her own hand blade you and rely on luck?"
translations.idiomatic: She vowed to kill him with her own hand rather than trust to chance."

sentences.zh: ”阴巿名刀，挟长持短，昼夜哀酸，志在杀寿。

translations.literal: She secretly bought a famous blade in the market, carried long and short weapons, wept day and night in bitter grief, her will fixed on killing Shou.
translations.idiomatic: She bought a fine sword and nursed her resolve night and day.

sentences.zh: 寿为人凶豪，闻娥亲之言，更乘马带刀，乡人皆畏惮之。

translations.literal: Shou by nature was fierce and bold; hearing Eqin's words, he all the more rode horse bearing blade; the villagers all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou rode armed through the district, terrifying the neighbors.

sentences.zh: 比邻有徐氏妇，忧娥亲不能制，恐逆见中害，每谏止之，曰：“李寿，男子也，凶恶有素，加今备卫在身。

translations.literal: A neighboring woman surnamed Xu, fearing Eqin could not overcome him and might instead be harmed, often remonstrated to stop her, saying: "Li Shou is a man, fierce and evil by nature, and now is on guard with weapons on his person.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor Mrs. Xu urged her to abandon the plan, saying a woman could not match an armed bully.

sentences.zh: 赵虽有猛烈之志，而强弱不敌。

translations.literal: Although Zhao has fierce resolve, strong and weak do not match.
translations.idiomatic: Strength was not on her side.

sentences.zh: 邂逅不制，则为重受祸於寿，绝灭门户，痛辱不轻也。

translations.literal: If by chance you cannot control him, you will instead suffer heavy disaster from Shou, cut off your gate and lineage—grief and shame would not be light.
translations.idiomatic: Failure would destroy her house and deepen her shame.

sentences.zh: 原详举动，为门户之计。

translations.literal: I beg you weigh your movements and plan for your gate."
translations.idiomatic: She begged her to think of the family line."

sentences.zh: ”娥亲曰：“父母之仇，不同天地共日月者也。

translations.literal: Eqin said: "A parent's enemy is not one who shares heaven and earth or sun and moon."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhao replied that a father's murderer cannot coexist under heaven.

sentences.zh: 李寿不死，娥亲视息世间，活复何求！

translations.literal: While Li Shou does not die, Eqin draws breath in the world—what more do I seek in living!
translations.idiomatic: While Li Shou lived she had no reason to live.

sentences.zh: 今虽三弟早死，门户泯绝，而娥亲犹在，岂可假手於人哉！

translations.literal: Now although three younger brothers died early and the gate is extinguished, yet Eqin still lives—how could I leave the deed to another's hand!
translations.idiomatic: Though her brothers were gone she would not delegate vengeance.

sentences.zh: 若以卿心况我，则李寿不可得杀；

translations.literal: If one judges by your heart toward me, then Li Shou cannot be obtained to kill;
translations.idiomatic: Mrs. Xu's caution would leave the killer alive;

sentences.zh: 论我之心，寿必为我所杀明矣。

translations.literal: judging by my heart, Shou is sure to be killed by me—that is clear."
translations.idiomatic: in Lady Zhao's mind Li Shou was already a dead man."

sentences.zh: ”夜数磨砺所持刀讫，扼腕切齿，悲涕长叹，家人及邻里咸共笑之。

translations.literal: By night she repeatedly sharpened the blade she held, wrung her wrist, gnashed her teeth, wept and sighed long; family and neighbors together laughed at her.
translations.idiomatic: She honed her blade nightly while kin and neighbors mocked her.

sentences.zh: 娥亲谓左右曰：“卿等笑我，直以我女弱不能杀寿故也。

translations.literal: Eqin said to those about her: "You laugh at me only because I am a weak woman and cannot kill Shou.
translations.idiomatic: She told them they laughed because they thought a woman could not kill Li Shou.

sentences.zh: 要当以寿颈血污此刀刃，令汝辈见之。

translations.literal: I shall yet stain this blade's edge with the blood of Shou's neck and let you all see it."
translations.idiomatic: She would prove them wrong with Li Shou's blood on the steel."

sentences.zh: ”遂弃家事，乘鹿车伺寿。

translations.literal: Thereupon she abandoned household affairs, rode a deer cart, and watched for Shou.
translations.idiomatic: She abandoned her home and stalked him in a deer cart.

sentences.zh: 至光和二年二月上旬，以白日清时，於都亭之前，与寿相遇，便下车扣寿马，叱之。

translations.literal: In the second month, first third of the second month of the second year of Guanghe, in the clear daylight of a bright day, before the metropolitan pavilion she met Shou, dismounted, seized Shou's horse's bit, and shouted at him.
translations.idiomatic: On a clear morning in Guanghe 2 she seized his bridle at the pavilion and denounced him.

sentences.zh: 寿惊愕，回马欲走。

translations.literal: Shou was startled and turned his horse wishing to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou tried to wheel his horse and flee.

sentences.zh: 娥亲奋刀斫之，并伤其马。

translations.literal: Eqin raised her blade and hacked him, also wounding his horse.
translations.idiomatic: She hacked at him and wounded his mount.

sentences.zh: 马惊，寿挤道边沟中。

translations.literal: The horse panicked; Shou was squeezed into the ditch beside the road.
translations.idiomatic: The horse threw him into the roadside ditch.

sentences.zh: 娥亲寻复就地斫之，探中树兰，折所持刀。

translations.literal: Eqin sought again to hack him where he lay; she struck a tamarisk and broke the blade she held.
translations.idiomatic: She struck again but hit a tamarisk and broke her sword.

sentences.zh: 寿被创未死，娥亲因前欲取寿所佩刀杀寿，寿护刀瞋目大呼，跳梁而起。

translations.literal: Shou was wounded but not dead; Eqin thereupon advanced wishing to take the blade Shou wore to kill Shou; Shou guarded the blade, glared with eyes and shouted greatly, and leaped up.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded, Li Shou still guarded his dagger and tried to rise roaring.

sentences.zh: 娥亲乃挺身奋手，左抵其额，右樁其喉，反覆盘旋，应手而倒。

translations.literal: Eqin thereupon straightened her body, stretched her hands, with the left pressed his forehead, with the right rammed his throat, whirled and twisted, and he fell at the stroke of her hand.
translations.idiomatic: She closed, pinned his throat, and strangled him down.

sentences.zh: 遂拔其刀以截寿头，持诣都亭，归罪有司，徐步诣狱，辞颜不变。

translations.literal: Thereupon she drew his blade to cut off Shou's head, carried it to the metropolitan pavilion, returned guilt to the authorities, and walked slowly to prison, her expression unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: She took his head to the authorities and walked calmly to prison.

sentences.zh: 时禄福长汉阳尹嘉不忍论娥亲，即解印绶去官，弛法纵之。

translations.literal: At that time the Lufu magistrate Yin Jia of Hanyang could not bear to judge Eqin; immediately he removed seal-ribbons, left office, relaxed the law and released her.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Yin Jia resigned rather than sentence her and let her go.

sentences.zh: 娥亲曰：“仇塞身死，妾之明分也。

translations.literal: Eqin said: "When the enemy is cut off and the body dies, that is my clear lot.
translations.idiomatic: She said vengeance done, she was ready to die.

sentences.zh: 治狱制刑，君之常典也。

translations.literal: To try cases and apply punishments is your lordship's constant code.
translations.idiomatic: Trials were the magistrate's duty.

sentences.zh: 何敢贪生以枉官法？

translations.literal: How dare I cling to life and bend the law of officials?"
translations.idiomatic: She would not live by bending the statute."

sentences.zh: ”乡人闻之，倾城奔往，观者如堵焉，莫不为之悲喜慷慨嗟叹也。

translations.literal: The villagers hearing it, the whole city ran to look; spectators were like a wall; none did not for her feel joy and sorrow, generous passion and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: The whole town crowded to watch, moved to tears and admiration.

sentences.zh: 守尉不敢公纵，阴语使去，以便宜自匿。

translations.literal: The warden and captain did not dare openly release her; secretly they told her to leave and on her own convenience hide.
translations.idiomatic: Local officers whispered that she should flee.

sentences.zh: 娥亲抗声大言曰：“枉法逃死，非妾本心。

translations.literal: Eqin raised her voice in great words, saying: "To twist the law and escape death is not this handmaid's heart.
translations.idiomatic: She refused to flee and stain the law.

sentences.zh: 今仇人已雪，死则妾分，乞得归法以全国体。

translations.literal: Now the enemy is wiped out; to die is this handmaid's lot; I beg to return to the law to preserve the integrity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: She asked to accept execution to vindicate the code.

sentences.zh: 虽复万死，於娥亲毕足，不敢贪生为明廷负也。

translations.literal: Though I die ten thousand deaths, for Eqin it is fully enough—I dare not cling to life and betray the enlightened court."
translations.idiomatic: She would die ten thousand deaths rather than live by betraying the court."

sentences.zh: ”尉故不听所执，娥亲复言曰：“匹妇虽微，犹知宪制。

translations.literal: The captain therefore would not heed what she held to; Eqin again spoke, saying: "Though a common woman be slight, still she knows the statutes."
translations.idiomatic: The warden would not take her into custody; she insisted that even a humble woman knew the law.

sentences.zh: 杀人之罪，法所不纵。

translations.literal: The crime of killing a man is what the law does not indulge.
translations.idiomatic: Murder was not something the code could overlook.

sentences.zh: 今既犯之，义无可逃。

translations.literal: Now that I have violated it, by righteousness there is no escape.
translations.idiomatic: Having killed, she could not in honor flee punishment.

sentences.zh: 乞就刑戮，陨身朝巿，肃明王法，娥亲之原也。

translations.literal: I beg to submit to execution and mutilation, cast away my body in the morning market, to make clear the king's law—that is Eqin's wish."
translations.idiomatic: She asked to die in the public square to vindicate the statute—that was her wish."

sentences.zh: ”辞气愈厉，面无惧色。

translations.literal: Her words and spirit grew more severe; her face showed no fear.
translations.idiomatic: Her voice grew sharper and her face showed no fear.

sentences.zh: 尉知其难夺，强载还家。

translations.literal: The captain knew he could not sway her and forced her into a cart to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The warden gave up arguing and sent her home by cart.

sentences.zh: 凉州刺史周洪、酒泉太守刘班等并共表上，称其烈义，刊石立碑，显其门闾。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Liangzhou Zhou Hong, the governor of Jiuquan Liu Ban, and others jointly memorialized upward, praising her fierce righteousness, carved a stone and raised a stele, and made manifest her gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hong of Liangzhou and Liu Ban of Jiuquan memorialized the throne, praised her valor, and raised a stone at her gate.

sentences.zh: 太常弘农张奂贵尚所履，以束帛二十端礼之。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhang Huan of Hongnong esteemed the conduct she had trod and with twenty bolts of silk bowed to her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan, grand master of ceremonies, honored her with twenty rolls of silk.

sentences.zh: 海内闻之者，莫不改容赞善，高大其义。

translations.literal: Those within the seas who heard none failed to change expression and praise good, exalting her righteousness as lofty.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard the story praised her moral stature.

sentences.zh: 故黄门侍郎安定梁宽追述娥亲，为其作传。

translations.literal: Therefore the former Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Liang Kuan of Anding later narrated Eqin and for her composed a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Kuan of Anding later wrote her biography.

sentences.zh: 玄晏先生以为父母之仇，不与共天地，盖男子之所为也。

translations.literal: Master Xuanyuan held that a parent's enemy is not one with whom one shares heaven and earth—that is generally what men do.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator Xuanxuan observed that avenging a parent was usually a man's duty.

sentences.zh: 而娥亲以女弱之微，念父辱之酷痛，感仇党之凶言，奋剑仇颈，人马俱摧，塞亡父之怨魂，雪三弟之永恨，近古已来，未之有也。

translations.literal: Yet Eqin, though slight as a weak woman, remembered her father's cruel shame, was moved by the fierce words of the enemy faction, raised a sword against the enemy's neck, man and horse both were destroyed, blocked the wandering resentful soul of her dead father, and wiped away the everlasting hatred of three younger brothers—since near antiquity there has not been such a one.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this woman, stirred by her father's murder and the enemy's taunts, killed Li Shou in single combat—unprecedented in recent ages.

sentences.zh: 诗云“修我戈矛，与子同仇”，娥亲之谓也。〉

translations.literal: The Classic says "Sharpen my spear and halberd—I share your enemy"—that speaks of Eqin.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Odes line on sharing the lord's enemies applies to her.〉

sentences.zh: 阎温字伯俭，天水西城人也。

translations.literal: Yan Wen, courtesy name Bojian, was a man of Xicheng in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wen, courtesy name Bojian, came from Xicheng in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 以凉州别驾守上邽令。

translations.literal: By office he was Liangzhou aide-de-camp and acting magistrate of Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Liangzhou aide and acting magistrate of Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 马超走奔上邽，郡人任养等举众迎之。

translations.literal: Ma Chao fled to Shanggui; the county people Ren Yang and others raised the multitude to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Chao fled to Shanggui, Ren Yang and others opened the city to him.

sentences.zh: 温止之，不能禁，乃驰还州。

translations.literal: Wen tried to stop them but could not forbid them; thereupon he galloped back to the province.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wen could not stop the rising and raced back to the provincial seat.

sentences.zh: 超复围州所治冀城甚急，州乃遣温密出，告急於夏侯渊。

translations.literal: Chao again besieged the province seat at Jicheng very urgently; the province thereupon dispatched Wen secretly out to report emergency to Xiahou Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao besieged Jicheng; the province sent Yan Wen secretly to beg relief from Xiahou Yuan.

sentences.zh: 贼围数重，温夜从水中潜出。

translations.literal: The bandits' siege was several layers deep; Wen by night slipped out through the water.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped through the enemy cordon by night along the watercourse.

sentences.zh: 明日，贼见其迹，遣人追遮之，於显亲界得温，执还诣超。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits saw his tracks and sent men to pursue and intercept him; at the border of Xianqin they caught Wen and brought him back to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Trackers caught him next day at the Xianqin border and brought him to Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 超解其缚，谓曰：“今成败可见，足下为孤城请救而执於人手，义何所施？

translations.literal: Chao loosed his bonds and said to him: "Now success or defeat can be seen; you went to beg rescue for an isolated city yet were taken in another's hand—where is righteousness to be applied?
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao freed him and sneered that his mission had failed.

sentences.zh: 若从吾言，反谓城中，东方无救，此转祸为福之计也。

translations.literal: If you follow my words, return and tell the city that there is no relief from the east—this is the plan to turn misfortune into fortune.
translations.idiomatic: If he would shout to the city that no help was coming, Ma Chao would spare him.

sentences.zh: 不然，今为戮矣。

translations.literal: If not, now you will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise he would die at once."

sentences.zh: ”温伪许之，超乃载温诣城下。

translations.literal: Wen falsely promised; Chao thereupon carried Wen beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wen feigned agreement; Ma Chao had him driven under the walls.

sentences.zh: 温向城大呼曰：“大军不过三日至，勉之！

translations.literal: Wen toward the city shouted greatly, saying: "The great army will arrive within three days—strive on!
translations.idiomatic: He shouted that relief would arrive within three days.

sentences.zh: ”城中皆泣，称万岁。

translations.literal: Those within the city all wept and cried long life.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders wept and cheered.

sentences.zh: 超怒数之曰：“足下不为命计邪？

translations.literal: Chao angrily rebuked him, saying: "Do you not plan for your life?"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao raged at him for throwing away his life.

sentences.zh: ”温不应。

translations.literal: Wen did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wen was silent.

sentences.zh: 时超攻城久不下，故徐诱温，冀其改意。

translations.literal: At that time Chao had long been unable to take the city by attack; therefore he slowly enticed Wen, hoping he would change his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao had stalled before the walls and hoped to turn him.

sentences.zh: 复谓温曰：“城中故人，有欲与吾同者不？

translations.literal: Again he said to Wen: "Are there in the city old friends who wish to join with me?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether anyone inside wished to defect.

sentences.zh: ”温又不应。

translations.literal: Wen again did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wen still said nothing.

sentences.zh: 遂切责之，温曰：“夫事君有死无贰，而卿乃欲令长者出不义之言，吾岂苟生者乎？

translations.literal: Thereupon he sharply rebuked him; Wen said: "Serving a lord is to die without a second thought—yet you wish to make an elder speak unrighteous words—am I one who clings to life?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wen replied that a loyal minister dies for his lord and would not utter treason to save himself.

sentences.zh: ”超遂杀之。

translations.literal: Chao thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao executed him.

sentences.zh: 先是，河右扰乱，隔绝不通，敦煌太守马艾卒官，府又无丞。

translations.literal: Before this, the west of the river was in turmoil, cut off and without communication; the Dunhuang governor Ma Ai died in office, and the headquarters moreover had no assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Hexi corridor was cut off; Dunhuang's governor Ma Ai had died without an assistant in office.

sentences.zh: 功曹张恭素有学行，郡人推行长史事，恩信甚著，乃遣子就东诣太祖，请太守。

translations.literal: The merit clerk Zhang Gong had long had learning and conduct; the county people advanced him to handle chief clerk affairs; his grace and trust were very manifest; thereupon he sent his son Jiu east to the Grand Progenitor to request a governor.
translations.idiomatic: Merit clerk Zhang Gong, respected locally, sent his son Zhang Jiu east to Cao Cao to ask for a new governor.

sentences.zh: 时酒泉黄华、张掖张进各据其郡，欲与恭

translations.literal: At that time Huang Hua of Jiuquan and Zhang Jin of Zhangye each held their commanderies and wished with Gong
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hua and Zhang Jin each held their cities and meant to join Zhang Gong

translations.literal: (Ai) — gloss on the preceding name.
translations.idiomatic: The text glosses the name as Ai.

sentences.zh: 并势。

translations.literal: in combined strength.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to combine their forces against the court.

sentences.zh: 就至酒泉，为华所拘执，劫以白刃。

translations.literal: When Jiu reached Jiuquan, Hua seized and held him, coercing him with naked blades.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hua seized Zhang Jiu at Jiuquan and threatened him with swords.

sentences.zh: 就终不回，私与恭疏曰：“大人率厉敦煌，忠义显然，岂以就在困危之中而替之哉？

translations.literal: Jiu to the end would not turn; privately he wrote Gong a letter, saying: "You, sir, lead and encourage Dunhuang—loyalty and righteousness are clear—how could you because Jiu is in peril and crisis replace them?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiu refused to yield and wrote secretly urging his father not to ransom him.

sentences.zh: 昔乐羊食子，李通覆家，经国之臣，宁怀妻孥邪？

translations.literal: Formerly Yue Yang ate his son; Li Tong overturned his household—ministers who order the state—do they cherish wife and children?
translations.idiomatic: He cited Yue Yang and Li Tong as men who put the state before family.

sentences.zh: 今大军垂至，但当促兵以掎之耳；

translations.literal: Now the great army is about to arrive—you need only press troops to pinch them;
translations.idiomatic: The imperial host was near; Zhang Gong need only hurry troops to pinch the rebels;

sentences.zh: 原不以下流之爱，使就有恨於黄壤也。

translations.literal: I beg you not for love of a lesser stream let Jiu harbor resentment in the yellow earth."
translations.idiomatic: he begged his father not to spare him from sentiment."

sentences.zh: ”恭即遣从弟华攻酒泉沙头、乾齐二县。

translations.literal: Gong immediately dispatched his cousin Hua to attack the two counties of Shatou and Ganqi in Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gong sent his kinsman to strike Jiuquan's Shatou and Ganqi.

sentences.zh: 恭又连兵寻继华后，以为首尾之援。

translations.literal: Gong again linked troops continuing after Hua to be head-and-tail aid.
translations.idiomatic: He followed with a second column in mutual support.

sentences.zh: 别遣铁骑二百，迎吏官属，东缘酒泉北塞，径出张掖北河，逢迎太守尹奉。

translations.literal: Separately he dispatched two hundred armored horse to meet the clerk-officials' dependents, east along the northern border of Jiuquan, straight out to the northern river of Zhangye, to meet and welcome Governor Yin Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred cavalry escorted the new governor Yin Feng in along the northern road.

sentences.zh: 於是张进须黄华之助；

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang Jin awaited Huang Hua's aid;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin waited for Huang Hua's help;

sentences.zh: 华欲救进，西顾恭兵，恐急击其后，遂诣金城太守苏则降。

translations.literal: Hua wished to save Jin but looking west feared Gong's troops would urgently strike his rear; thereupon he went to Jincheng governor Su Ze and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hua dared not move for fear of Zhang Gong behind him and surrendered to Su Ze at Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 就竟平安。

translations.literal: Jiu in the end was safe and sound.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiu survived.

sentences.zh: 奉得之官。

translations.literal: Feng obtained office.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Feng took up his post.

sentences.zh: 黄初二年，下诏褒扬，赐恭爵关内侯，拜西域戊己校尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu an edict down praised him, granted Gong the noble rank of secondary marquis within the passes, and appointed him colonel of the gengji garrison of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2 an edict praised Zhang Gong, enfeoffed him as secondary marquis, and named him colonel of the Western Regions garrison.

sentences.zh: 数岁徵还，将授以侍臣之位，而以子就代焉。

translations.literal: Several years later he was summoned back and was about to be given a palace attendant post, but his son Jiu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled for court office but sent his son to replace him in the west.

sentences.zh: 恭至敦煌，固辞疾笃。

translations.literal: Gong reached Dunhuang and firmly declined on grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: At Dunhuang he pleaded serious illness and declined further service.

sentences.zh: 太和中卒，赠执金吾。

translations.literal: In the Taihe years he died and was posthumously gifted Bearer of the Golden Mace.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Taihe era and was posthumously named bearer of the golden mace.

sentences.zh: 就后为金城太守，父子著称於西州。

translations.literal: Jiu later became governor of Jincheng; father and son were famed in the western province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiu later governed Jincheng; father and son were renowned in the west.

sentences.zh: 〈《世语》曰：就子斅，字祖文，弘毅有幹正，晋武帝世为广汉太守。

translations.literal: The Shiyu says: Jiu's son Xue, courtesy name Zuwen, was resolute and upright; in Emperor Wu of Jin's reign he was governor of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu records Zhang Jiu's son Zhang Xue as governor of Guanghan under Jin Wu.

sentences.zh: 王濬在益州，受中制募兵讨吴，无虎符，斅收濬从事列上，由此召斅还。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun was in Yizhou he received inner orders to raise troops against Wu without a tiger tally; Xue arrested Wang Jun's aide and reported it upward; thereby Xue was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xue arrested an aide of Wang Jun for raising troops without the proper tally.

sentences.zh: 帝责斅：“何不密启而便收从事？

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Xue: "Why did you not secretly memorialize but straightway arrest the aide?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why he had not reported secretly first.

sentences.zh: ”斅曰：“蜀汉绝远，刘备尝用之。

translations.literal: Xue said: "Shu and Han are utterly remote; Liu Bei once used such license.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xue answered that the Shu region was remote and had seen such abuses before.

sentences.zh: 辄收，臣犹以为轻。

translations.literal: To arrest outright I still thought light.
translations.idiomatic: Arresting the man outright was already lenient.

sentences.zh: ”帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 官至匈奴中郎将。

translations.literal: His office reached general of the household against the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general of the household against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 斅子固，字元安，有斅风，为黄门郎，早卒。

translations.literal: Xue's son Gu, courtesy name Yuan'an, had Xue's manner; he was gentleman of the Yellow Gates and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Gu, like him in character, was a gentleman of the Yellow Gates and died young.

sentences.zh: 斅，一本作勃。

translations.literal: Xue—in one edition is written Bo.
translations.idiomatic: One manuscript writes his name as Bo instead of Xue.

sentences.zh: 《魏略勇侠传》载孙宾硕、祝公道、杨阿若、鲍出等四人，宾硕虽汉人，而鱼豢编之魏书，盖以其人接魏，事义相类故也。

translations.literal: The Wei lüe Biography of Brave Knights carries four men: Sun Binshuo, Zhu Gongdao, Yang Aruo, and Bao Chu; although Binshuo was a Han man, Yu Huan compiled him in the Wei book—because those persons touched Wei and the affairs and righteousness were of a kind.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Yu Huan's Wei lüe grouped Han-era bravoes with Wei for thematic reasons.

sentences.zh: 论其行节，皆庞、阎之流。

translations.literal: Judging their conduct and integrity, all are of the stream of Pang and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Their conduct matched Pang Jun and Yan Wen.

sentences.zh: 其祝公道一人，已见《贾逵传》。

translations.literal: Of Zhu Gongdao alone, he is already seen in the biography of Jia Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gongdao is already treated in Jia Kui's biography.

sentences.zh: 今列宾硕等三人于后。

translations.literal: Now I list Binshuo and three others after.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Binshuo and three others are appended below.

sentences.zh: ◎孙宾硕者，北海人也，家素贫。

translations.literal: Sun Binshuo was a man of the North Sea; his family had always been poor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Binshuo of Beihai came from a poor family.

sentences.zh: 当汉桓帝时，常侍左悺、唐衡等权侔人主。

translations.literal: In the time of Han Huan, the regular attendants Zuo Guan, Tang Heng, and others had power equal to the lord of men.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huan, eunuchs such as Zuo Guan and Tang Heng rivaled the throne.

sentences.zh: 延熹中，衡弟为京兆虎牙都尉，秩比二千石，而统属郡。

translations.literal: In the Yanxi years, Heng's younger brother was colonel of the tiger fangs of the capital region, rank equal to two thousand piculs, yet subordinate to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi Tang Heng's brother held the capital tiger-fang colonelcy at two thousand piculs but answered to the commandery.

sentences.zh: 衡弟初之官，不脩敬於京兆尹，入门不持版，郡功曹赵息呵廊下曰：“虎牙仪如属城，何得放臂入府门？

translations.literal: When Heng's younger brother first came to office he did not show respect to the capital region governor; entering the gate he did not hold his tablet; the commandery merit clerk Zhao Xi in the corridor under the eaves shouted: "The tiger fangs' ceremony is like a dependent city—how dare you swing your arms through the government gate?"
translations.idiomatic: The new colonel snubbed the governor; clerk Zhao Xi humiliated him at the gate.

sentences.zh: ”促收其主簿。

translations.literal: He urged seizure of his chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his chief clerk seized.

sentences.zh: 衡弟顾促取版，既入见尹，尹欲脩主人，敕外为市买。

translations.literal: Heng's younger brother looked about in haste to fetch a tablet; having entered to see the governor, the governor wished to play host and ordered outside to go to market to buy.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel fetched his tablet; the governor meant to entertain him and sent for provisions.

sentences.zh: 息又启云：“

translations.literal: Xi again reported, saying: "
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xi reported again, saying: "

translations.literal: (Zuo) — marginal gloss.
translations.idiomatic: A marginal gloss marks the surname as Zuo.

sentences.zh: 悺子弟，来为虎牙，非德选，不足为特酤买，宜随中舍菜食而已。

translations.literal: Guan's son and younger brother has come as tiger fangs—not a virtuous selection—not worthy of special wine purchase; plain fare from the middle kitchen is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Guan's kinsman has come as tiger fangs—not a virtuous selection—not worthy of special wine purchase; plain fare from the middle kitchen is enough."

sentences.zh: ”及其到官，遣吏奉笺谢尹，息又敕门，言“无常见此无阴兒辈子弟邪，用其笺记为通乎？

translations.literal: When he reached office he sent a clerk with a note to thank the governor; Xi again ordered the gate, saying: "Is it never proper to see these castrated fellows' sons and younger brothers—use their note as pass?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xi then blocked his thank-you letter at the gate with insults.

sentences.zh: ”晚乃通之，又不得即令报。

translations.literal: Only late was it passed through, nor could he immediately order a reply.
translations.idiomatic: The message was delayed and left unanswered.

sentences.zh: 衡弟皆知之，甚恚，欲灭诸赵。

translations.literal: Heng's younger brothers all knew it and were very angry and wished to exterminate the various Zhaos.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang brothers resolved to wipe out the Zhao clan.

sentences.zh: 因书与衡，求为京兆尹，旬月之间，得为之。

translations.literal: Therefore they wrote to Heng asking to be capital region governor; within a month or so they obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: They had Tang Heng secure the capital governorship within weeks.

sentences.zh: 息自知前过，乃逃走。

translations.literal: Xi knew his former fault and thereupon fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xi fled.

sentences.zh: 时息从父仲台，见为凉州刺史，於是衡为诏徵仲台，遣归。

translations.literal: At that time Xi's father's younger brother Zhongtai was then Inspector of Liangzhou; thereupon Heng forged an edict to summon Zhongtai and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Heng forged a recall of Zhao Zhongtai from Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遂诏中都官及郡部督邮，捕诸赵尺兒以上，及仲台皆杀之，有藏者与同罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict to the capital officials and commandery department overseers to seize all Zhao males above ruler length and Zhongtai and kill them; whoever harbored them shared the crime.
translations.idiomatic: An order went out to slaughter every Zhao male and anyone who sheltered them.

sentences.zh: 时息从父岐为皮氏长，闻有家祸，因从官舍逃，走之河间，变姓字，又转诣北海，著絮巾布袴，常於市中贩胡饼。

translations.literal: At that time Xi's father's younger brother Qi was magistrate of Pishi; hearing of the family disaster, he fled from the official quarters, ran to Hejian, changed surname and personal name, and again shifted to Beihai, wearing cotton cap and cloth trousers, constantly in the market selling Hu cakes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qi fled to Beihai in disguise and sold cakes in the market.

sentences.zh: 宾硕时年二十餘，乘犊车，将骑入市。

translations.literal: Binshuo was then more than twenty years old; riding a calf cart with horsemen he entered the market.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Binshuo, in his twenties, drove into the market with escorts.

sentences.zh: 观见岐，疑其非常人也。

translations.literal: Seeing Qi, he suspected he was not an ordinary person.
translations.idiomatic: He saw Zhao Qi and sensed he was no ordinary peddler.

sentences.zh: 因问之曰：“自有饼邪，贩之邪？

translations.literal: Therefore he asked him, saying: "Do you yourself make the cakes or do you resell them?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether the cakes were his own or resale goods.

sentences.zh: ”岐曰：“贩之。

translations.literal: Qi said: "I resell them."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qi said he resold them.

sentences.zh: ”宾硕曰：“买几钱？

translations.literal: Binshuo said: "At what price do you buy? At what price do you sell?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Binshuo asked his margins.

sentences.zh: 卖几钱？

translations.literal: Qi said: "I buy at thirty; I sell also at thirty."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qi said he bought and sold at the same thirty.

sentences.zh: ”岐曰：“买三十，卖亦三十。

translations.literal: Binshuo said: "Looking at the gentleman's bearing, you do not resemble a cake seller—there must be some reason!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Binshuo said no honest merchant would sell at cost.

sentences.zh: ”宾硕曰：“视处士之望，非似卖饼者，殆有故！

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened the rear door of the cart, looked back at the two horsemen he led, and ordered them to dismount and help him up.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the cart, ordered his riders to lift Zhao Qi in,

sentences.zh: ”乃开车后户，顾所将两骑，令下马扶上之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened the rear door of the cart, looked back at the two horsemen he led, and ordered them to dismount and help him up.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the back of the cart, signaled his two escorts, and had them dismount and lift Zhao Qi aboard.

sentences.zh: 时岐以为是唐氏耳目也，甚怖，面失色。

translations.literal: At that time Qi thought these were Tang's eyes and ears and was very afraid, his face losing color.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qi took them for Tang Heng's spies, was terrified, and went pale.

sentences.zh: 宾硕闭车后户，下前襜，谓之曰：“视处士状貌，既非贩饼者，加今面色变动，即不有重怨，则当亡命。

translations.literal: Binshuo closed the rear cart door, lowered the front apron, and said to him: "Looking at the gentleman's appearance, you are not a cake seller; moreover now your face has changed color—you either have a deep grievance or must be a fugitive."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Binshuo shut the rear door, let the front apron fall, and said, "From your bearing you are no cake seller, and your color has changed—you carry either a deep blood debt or you are a fugitive."

sentences.zh: 我北海孙宾硕也，阖门百口，又有百岁老母在堂，势能相度者也，终不相负，必语我以实。

translations.literal: I am Sun Binshuo of Beihai; my whole gate is a hundred mouths and moreover there is a hundred-year-old mother in the hall—by force I can measure the situation—I will never betray you—you must tell me the truth.
translations.idiomatic: I am Sun Binshuo of Beihai. A hundred souls look to my gate, and a mother of a hundred years sits in our hall. I have the means to judge your case and I will not betray you—you must tell me the truth.

sentences.zh: ”岐乃具告之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qi fully told him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qi then told him everything.

sentences.zh: 宾硕遂载岐驱归。

translations.literal: Binshuo thereupon loaded Qi and drove back.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Binshuo put him in the cart and drove him home.

sentences.zh: 住车门外，先入，白母言：“今日出得死友在外，当来入拜。

translations.literal: Stopping the cart outside the gate, he first entered and told his mother, saying: "Today outside I have obtained a friend who would die for me—he must come in to bow."
translations.idiomatic: He halted outside the gate, went in first, and said to his mother, "Today I found a friend worth dying for—he is outside and should come in to pay his respects."

sentences.zh: ”乃出，延岐入，椎牛锺酒，快相娱乐。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went out, extended Qi to enter, slaughtered an ox and poured wine, and they joyfully entertained each other.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought Zhao Qi inside, slaughtered an ox, poured the wine, and they feasted together in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 一二日，因载著别田舍，藏置衤复壁中。

translations.literal: After a day or two, he therefore loaded him and brought him to another farmstead, hiding and placing him in a double wall.
translations.idiomatic: A day or two later he moved Zhao Qi to a remote farm and hid him between hollow walls.

sentences.zh: 后数岁，唐衡及弟皆死。

translations.literal: Several years later, Tang Heng and his younger brothers all died.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Tang Heng and his brothers were all dead.

sentences.zh: 岐乃得出，还本郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qi was able to come out and return to his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qi could emerge and return to his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 三府并辟，展转仕进，至郡守、刺史、太仆，而宾硕亦从此显名於东国，仕至豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The three bureaus together summoned him; he shifted from post to post until governor, inspector, and grand coachman, while Binshuo from this also became famous in the eastern states, reaching office as Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: The three high offices summoned Zhao Qi; he rose through governor, inspector, and grand coachman, while Sun Binshuo won fame in the east and became inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 初平末，宾硕以东方饥荒，南客荆州。

translations.literal: At the end of Chuping, Binshuo because of famine in the east became a guest south in Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Chuping Sun Binshuo fled famine in the east and took refuge in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 至兴平中，赵岐以太仆持节使安慰天下，南诣荆州，乃复与宾硕相遇，相对流涕。

translations.literal: By the middle of Xingping, Zhao Qi as grand coachman bearing credentials went as envoy to console the realm; going south to Jing Province he again met Binshuo, and they faced each other weeping.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xingping era Zhao Qi, as grand coachman with imperial staff, toured the empire on a mission of consolation; when he reached Jingzhou he met Sun Binshuo again, and the two wept together.

sentences.zh: 岐为刘表陈其本末，由是益礼宾硕。

translations.literal: Qi for Liu Biao narrated the whole story from beginning to end; thereby Biao all the more treated Binshuo with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qi told Liu Biao the whole story of his rescue, and Liu Biao honored Sun Binshuo all the more.

sentences.zh: 顷之，宾硕病亡，岐在南，为行丧也。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Binshuo died of illness; Qi was in the south and conducted mourning for him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sun Binshuo died; Zhao Qi was still in the south and mourned him as for a kinsman.

sentences.zh: ◎杨阿若后名丰，字伯阳，酒泉人。

translations.literal: Yang Aruo—later his name was Feng, courtesy name Boyang, a man of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Aruo—later named Yang Feng, courtesy Boyang—was from Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 少游侠，常以报仇解怨为事，故时人为之号曰：“东市相斫杨阿若，西市相斫杨阿若。

translations.literal: In youth he roamed as knight-errant; constantly he took avenging grudves and undoing feuds as his business; therefore people of the time gave him the sobriquet: "East market hacks at each other—Yang Aruo; west market hacks at each other—Yang Aruo."
translations.idiomatic: As a young bravo he lived by blood feuds, so the saying ran: "East of the market they slash—Yang Aruo; west of the market they slash—Yang Aruo."

sentences.zh: ”至建安年中，太守徐揖诛郡中强族黄氏。

translations.literal: By the Jian'an years, Governor Xu Yi executed the powerful Huang clan of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an the governor Xu Yi put the great Huang family to death.

sentences.zh: 时黄昂得脱在外，乃以其家粟金数斛，募众得千餘人以攻揖。

translations.literal: At that time Huang Ang escaped outside; thereupon with several hu of grain and gold from his household he recruited a multitude and obtained more than a thousand men to attack Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ang escaped and spent his family grain and gold to raise over a thousand men against Xu Yi.

sentences.zh: 揖城守。

translations.literal: Yi defended the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi held the walls.

sentences.zh: 丰时在外，以昂为不义，乃告揖，捐妻子走诣张掖求救。

translations.literal: Feng was at that time outside; holding Ang unrighteous, he informed Yi, abandoned wife and children, and ran to Zhangye to beg rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng was away; deeming Huang Ang a villain, he warned Xu Yi, left his family, and raced to Zhangye for help.

sentences.zh: 会张掖又反，杀太守，而昂亦陷城杀揖，二郡合势。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhangye also rebelled, killed the governor, while Ang also took the city and killed Yi—the two commanderies united their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangye then revolted and killed its governor; Huang Ang stormed the city and killed Xu Yi, and the two districts joined forces.

sentences.zh: 昂恚丰不与己同，乃重募取丰，欲令张掖以麻系其头，生致之。

translations.literal: Ang resented Feng for not siding with him; thereupon he offered a heavy reward to seize Feng, wishing to have Zhangye tie hemp about his neck and bring him in alive.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ang hated Yang Feng for opposing him and offered a rich bounty to take him alive, even asking Zhangye to rope his neck with hemp.

sentences.zh: 丰遂逃走。

translations.literal: Feng thereupon fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng fled.

sentences.zh: 武威太守张猛假丰为都尉，使赍檄告酒泉，听丰为揖报雠。

translations.literal: Governor Zhang Meng of Wuwei lent Feng the office of chief commandant, ordered him to carry a proclamation to Jiuquan, and let Feng avenge Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Meng, governor of Wuwei, made Yang Feng acting chief commandant and sent him with a summons to Jiuquan to avenge Xu Yi.

sentences.zh: 丰遂单骑入南羌中，合众得千餘骑，从〔乐涫〕南山中出，指趋郡城。

translations.literal: Feng thereupon entered the Southern Qiang alone with one horse, united a host and obtained more than a thousand horse, came out from Mount Lequ in the southern mountains, and aimed straight for the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng rode alone into the Southern Qiang, raised a thousand cavalry, and burst from the Lequ range toward the city.

sentences.zh: 未到三十里，皆令骑下马，曳柴扬尘。

translations.literal: Before reaching thirty li he ordered all the riders to dismount, drag brushwood, and raise dust.
translations.idiomatic: Within thirty li of the city he had every man dismount and drag brush to raise a dust cloud.

sentences.zh: 酒泉郡人望见尘起，以为东大兵到，遂破散。

translations.literal: The people of Jiuquan commandery seeing dust rise thought a great eastern army had arrived and thereupon broke and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders saw the dust and fled, thinking a great host was coming from the east.

sentences.zh: 昂独走出，羌捕得昂，丰谓昂曰：“卿前欲生系我颈，今反为我所系，云何？

translations.literal: Ang alone ran out; the Qiang captured Ang; Feng said to Ang: "Earlier you wished to tie hemp about my neck alive—now instead you are tied by me—how is that?"
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ang fled alone; the Qiang seized him. Yang Feng said, "You wanted my neck in a noose—now the rope is on yours."

sentences.zh: ”昂惭谢，丰遂杀之。

translations.literal: Ang ashamed apologized; Feng thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ang begged pardon in shame; Yang Feng killed him.

sentences.zh: 时黄华在东，又还领郡。

translations.literal: At that time Huang Hua was in the east and again took charge of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hua was still in the east and had resumed the governorship.

sentences.zh: 丰畏华，复走依敦煌。

translations.literal: Feng feared Hua and again fled to take refuge at Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng feared Huang Hua and fled again to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 至黄初中，河西兴复，黄华降，丰乃还郡。

translations.literal: By the Huangchu years the Hexi was restored to order; Huang Hua surrendered, and Feng then returned to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hexi was pacified in Huangchu and Huang Hua submitted, Yang Feng came home.

sentences.zh: 郡举孝廉，州表其义勇，诏即拜驸马都尉。

translations.literal: The commandery raised him as filial and incorrupt; the province memorialized his courage and righteousness; an edict immediately appointed him commandant of the horse for the consorts.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt; the province praised his valor; the court named him commandant of the horse for the consorts.

sentences.zh: 后二十餘年，病亡。

translations.literal: More than twenty years later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness more than twenty years later.

sentences.zh: ◎鲍出字文才，京兆新丰人也。

translations.literal: Bao Chu, courtesy name Wencai, was a man of Xinfeng in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chu, courtesy Wencai, was from Xinfeng in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 少游侠。

translations.literal: In youth he roamed as knight-errant.
translations.idiomatic: He was a young knight-errant.

sentences.zh: 兴平中，三辅乱，出与老母兄弟五人家居本县，以饥饿，留其母守舍，相将行采蓬实，合得数升，使其二兄初、雅及其弟成持归，为母作食，独与小弟在后采蓬。

translations.literal: In the Xingping years the three adjuncts were in chaos; Chu with his old mother and five brothers of the household dwelt in his native county; because of hunger they left their mother to guard the house and together went to gather dodder seeds; altogether they obtained several sheng and ordered his two elder brothers Chu and Ya and younger brother Cheng to carry them back to cook food for their mother; he alone with the youngest brother remained behind gathering dodder.
translations.idiomatic: When Sanfu collapsed in Xingping, Bao Chu lived with his mother and four brothers. Starving, they left their mother at home while they foraged for dodder seeds; the two elder brothers and one younger brother carried the first bag home while Bao Chu and the youngest brother kept gathering.

sentences.zh: 初等到家，而啖人贼数十人已略其母，以绳贯其手掌，驱去。

translations.literal: When Chu and the others reached home, several tens of man-eating bandits had already plundered their mother, run a cord through her palms, and driven her away.
translations.idiomatic: When the brothers returned, dozens of cannibal raiders had seized their mother, strung cords through her hands, and marched her off.

sentences.zh: 初等怖恐，不敢追逐。

translations.literal: Chu and the others were terrified and did not dare pursue.
translations.idiomatic: The elder brothers were too afraid to follow.

sentences.zh: 须臾，出从后到，知母为贼所略，欲追贼。

translations.literal: After a moment Chu came from behind; learning his mother had been taken by bandits, he wished to pursue the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao Chu arrived and heard, he meant to chase them.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆云：“贼众，当如何？

translations.literal: The brothers all said: "The bandits are many—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: His brothers said the enemy was too many.

sentences.zh: ”出怒曰：“有母而使贼贯其手，将去煮啖之，用活何为？

translations.literal: Chu angrily said: "We have a mother yet let bandits string her hands—being driven off to be boiled and eaten—what use is living?"
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chu roared that while their mother was led away to be butchered, life was worthless.

sentences.zh: ”乃攘臂结衽独追之，行数里及贼。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rolled up his sleeves, tied his sash, and pursued alone; going several li he overtook the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He rolled his sleeves, tied his sash, and ran alone until he caught the band.

sentences.zh: 贼望见出，乃共布列待之。

translations.literal: The bandits seeing Chu thereupon together spread formation to await him.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders formed up to meet him.

sentences.zh: 出到，回从一头斫贼四五人。

translations.literal: When Chu arrived he wheeled from one end and hacked four or five bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He cut down four or five from one flank.

sentences.zh: 贼走，复合聚围出，出跳越围斫之，又杀十餘人。

translations.literal: The bandits fled, again gathered and surrounded Chu; Chu leaped the ring and hacked them, killing more than ten more.
translations.idiomatic: They scattered, regrouped, and surrounded him; he leaped the circle and killed another dozen.

sentences.zh: 时贼分布，驱出母前去。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits were scattered about, driving Chu's mother on ahead.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had split, dragging his mother forward.

sentences.zh: 贼连击出，不胜，乃走与前辈合。

translations.literal: The bandits struck at Chu in succession but could not overcome him; thereupon they fled to join the vanguard party.
translations.idiomatic: They could not bring him down and fled to rejoin the main body.

sentences.zh: 出复追击之，还见其母与比舍妪同贯相连，出遂复奋击贼。

translations.literal: Chu again pursued them; returning he saw his mother strung together with a neighboring old woman on one cord; Chu thereupon again fiercely struck the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued again, then saw his mother roped to a neighbor; he attacked once more.

sentences.zh: 贼问出曰：“卿欲何得？

translations.literal: The bandits asked Chu: "What do you want to obtain?"
translations.idiomatic: The bandits demanded what he wanted.

sentences.zh: ”出责数贼，指其母以示之，贼乃解还出母。

translations.literal: Chu rebuked the bandits, pointed to his mother to show them, and the bandits thereupon loosed and returned Chu's mother.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced them and pointed at his mother until they released her.

sentences.zh: 比舍妪独不解，遥望出求哀。

translations.literal: The neighboring old woman alone was not released; from afar she looked to Chu begging pity.
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor was still bound; she cried to him for mercy.

sentences.zh: 出复斫贼，贼谓出曰：“已还卿母，何为不止？

translations.literal: Chu again hacked the bandits; the bandits said to Chu: "We have already returned your mother—why do you not stop?"
translations.idiomatic: He struck again; they said they had given his mother back.

sentences.zh: ”出又指求哀妪：“此我嫂也。

translations.literal: Chu again pointed to the old woman begging pity: "This is my sister-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to the neighbor and said, "That is my sister-in-law."

sentences.zh: ”贼复解还之。

translations.literal: The bandits again released her.
translations.idiomatic: They freed her as well.

sentences.zh: 出得母还，遂相扶侍，客南阳。

translations.literal: Chu obtained his mother and returned; thereupon they supported each other and lodged as guests at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He brought his mother home, then the family moved south as guests at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 建安五年，关中始开，出来北归，而其母不能步行，兄弟欲共舆之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jian'an the passes of Guanzhong first opened; Chu came north to return, but his mother could not walk; the brothers wished together to carry her in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 5 the Guanzhong roads reopened; Bao Chu headed north, but his mother could not walk and his brothers wanted a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 出以舆车历山险危，不如负之安稳，乃以笼盛其母，独自负之，到乡里。

translations.literal: Chu held that a litter over mountain perils was not as safe as carrying her on his back; thereupon he put his mother in a basket and alone on his back bore her to the village.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chu thought a sedan unsafe on mountain tracks; he put his mother in a cage and carried her on his back all the way home.

sentences.zh: 乡里士大夫嘉其孝烈，欲荐州郡，郡辟召出，出曰：“田民不堪冠带。

translations.literal: The gentlemen of the village praised his filial fierceness and wished to recommend him to province and commandery; the commandery summoned Chu, and Chu said: "A field man cannot bear cap and sash."
translations.idiomatic: Local notables praised his devotion and tried to recommend him; the commandery summoned him, but he said a farmer was unfit for office.

sentences.zh: ”至青龙中，母年百餘岁乃终，出时年七十餘，行丧如礼，於今年八九十，才若五六十者。

translations.literal: By the Qinglong years his mother was more than a hundred when she finally died; Chu was then more than seventy yet observed mourning by the rites; today he is eighty or ninety yet seems only fifty or sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qinglong era his mother lived past a hundred; Bao Chu was over seventy when she died but still observed the full rites; even at eighty or ninety he looks like a man of fifty.

sentences.zh: 鱼豢曰：昔孔子叹颜回，以为三月不违仁者，盖观其心耳，孰如孙、祝菜色於市里，颠倒於牢狱，据有实事哉？

translations.literal: Yu Huan says: Formerly Kongzi sighed over Yan Hui, holding that for three months he did not depart from benevolence—he was looking at his heart; how does that compare to Sun and Zhu with their haggard faces in the market, overturned in prison, yet possessing solid deeds?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan asks whether Confucius' praise of Yan Hui matches men who actually suffered in markets and jails for their friends.

sentences.zh: 且夫濮阳周氏不敢匿迹，鲁之硃家不问情实，是何也？

translations.literal: Moreover the Zhou clan of Puyang did not dare hide traces, and the Zhu family of Lu did not ask into the facts—why was that?
translations.idiomatic: Why did the Zhou of Puyang and the Zhu of Lu act as they did?

sentences.zh: 惧祸之及，且心不安也。

translations.literal: They feared disaster reaching them and their hearts were not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: They feared reprisal and could not rest easy.

sentences.zh: 而太史公犹贵其竟脱季布，岂若二贤，厥义多乎？

translations.literal: Yet Grand Historian Sima Qian still esteems him for finally freeing Ji Bu—how can that compare to these two worthies, whose righteousness was the greater?
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian honors the man who freed Ji Bu—but are these two not more righteous?

sentences.zh: 今故远收孙、祝，而近录杨、鲍，既不欲其泯灭，且敦薄俗。

translations.literal: Therefore I have gathered Sun and Zhu from afar and recorded Yang and Bao near at hand, both not wishing them to perish and to chasten shallow custom.
translations.idiomatic: So I preserve Sun and Zhu from afar and Yang and Bao from near, to honor them and to rebuke mean ways.

sentences.zh: 至於鲍出，不染礼教，心痛意发，起於自然，迹虽在编户，与笃烈君子何以异乎？

translations.literal: As for Bao Chu, unstained by ritual teaching, pain in the heart and intent bursting forth arose from nature; though his traces are among the registered households, how does he differ from a steadfast gentleman of fierce integrity?
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chu, untaught by formal ritual, acted from raw natural duty; though a commoner, he was no different from a man of blazing integrity.

sentences.zh: 若夫杨阿若，少称任侠，长遂蹈义，自西徂东，摧讨逆节，可谓勇而有仁者也。〉

translations.literal: As for Yang Aruo, in youth he was called knight-errant; grown, he trod righteousness; from west to east he crushed rebellion—he may be called brave and humane.〉
translations.idiomatic: Yang Aruo was a bravo in youth and a man of right in maturity; he marched east and west crushing traitors—both brave and humane.〉

translations.literal: 【Appraisal (section rubric).】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal.

sentences.zh: 评曰：李典贵尚儒雅，义忘私隙，美矣。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Li Dian esteemed refined learning and forgot private grudges in the cause of duty—beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: The historian's verdict: Li Dian honored learning and set private quarrels aside for the common good—admirable.

sentences.zh: 李通、臧霸、文聘、吕虔镇卫州郡，并著威惠。

translations.literal: Li Tong, Zang Ba, Wen Pin, and Lü Qian guarded province and commandery and together showed awe and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong, Zang Ba, Wen Pin, and Lü Qian held the borders with a mix of severity and mercy.

sentences.zh: 许褚、典韦折冲左右，抑亦汉之樊哙也。

translations.literal: Xu Chu and Dian Wei broke the enemy at the ruler's flanks—they are also the Fan Kuai of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chu and Dian Wei were the Fan Kuai figures at Cao Cao's side.

sentences.zh: 庞德授命叱敌，有周苛之节。

translations.literal: Pang De received orders and reviled the foe—he had the integrity of Zhou Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Pang De gave his life defying the enemy, in the mold of Zhou Ke.

sentences.zh: 庞淯不惮伏剑，而诚感邻国。

translations.literal: Pang Jun did not shrink from baring a sword, yet his sincerity moved a neighboring state.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Jun risked the blade and his sincerity moved another realm.

sentences.zh: 阎温向城大呼，齐解、路之烈焉。

translations.literal: Yan Wen shouted toward the city—it matches the fierce steadfastness of Jie and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wen's shout beneath the walls recalls the steadfastness of Jie Zitui and Lu Zhonglian.
